text: The following is a presentation of the Arizona Cardinals Broadcast Network. We'll hear from players and coaches, [music] break down and react to the latest headlines surrounding the team, and take you to the annual Civic Matters send off. Cardinals Bird Watch starts right now, presented by SeatGeek. >> [music] >> Cardinals media day was this week. Get to see the players' personalities, have some fun photo shoots, and even an inside look at who's rocking new hairstyles. >> [clears throat] >> Trey McBride rocking the mullet. Zach is also a reminder that we are inching that much closer to the season. >> Yeah, I'm not sure if Mo McBride will be a nickname that sticks by the time training camp comes, but we try to be creative here on Cardinals Bird Watch. Zach Gershman, Danny Sorenson, and Danny, there's one box the guys needed to check off before training camp began. It was mandatory mini camp, full attendance. Everybody was in the house. >> The two players the media was keeping an eye on, quarterback Jacoby Brissett and outside linebacker Josh Sweat, who were both in attendance. Neither of them participated in any drills, and neither of them participated in voluntary OTA workouts. Because of that, head coach Michael LaFleur says that's the reason Joshua wasn't participating at mandatory mini camp was because he wasn't there for the first few phases of OTA. >> And in the case of Jacoby Brissett, reportedly he wants a situation change when it comes to his contract. The guys though, they all understand that it's a business at the end of the day. They still have their quarterbacks back. >> Yeah, I mean the guys are like super excited to see Jacoby back. You know, it was great and we all you know, he's going to come back today. Um but you know, that's our guy through and through, you know, we're we're behind him 100%. So, and it was it was it was it was good to see him. >> There's no surprise that Paris Johnson Jr., the franchise left tackle, is happy that his quarterback Jacoby Brissett is back in the building. When we talked to Paris, we asked him, "What's the biggest difference between year one Paris Johnson Jr. and year four?" And Danny said it's that leadership, having ownership of his play style. >> All players are continuously looking to improve every year. As an All-Pro tight end who's broken almost every positional franchise record, Jeremy Shockey's got a pretty good foundation heading into 2026 while still wanting more for himself. >> Really identifying who's covering you and how, you know, your route affects, you know, who's covering you and um I think that's something I've gotten better at and I'm still trying to get better at is who's who's who am I trying to beat on this play and um you know, how much free will do I have to beat this guy and um being able to digest that as fast as I can and be able to to play at a high level, play fast is is very important and um I just try to run fast and and get open and you know, hopefully the ball finds me and um more often than not it does. >> To say the least, 126 catches, more than 1,200 yards, 11 touchdowns for McBride last year. LaFleur says the sky's the limit for his number one tight end and Zach, even that might be too low based on what we've seen so far. >> Can you imagine if that is the floor for Tremaine McBride? It's pretty remarkable what he was able to do last year. And the ways that he's going to be utilized this year, well, that remains a mystery. Not everybody could see what Michael Bidwill and that offense is starting to look like. But Mack Wilson Sr. is one of the guys that can, and the linebacker could already see a difference. >> Yeah, I mean, it's a lot of eye candy. Um a lot of motions, obviously. Um can get you out of whack if you don't key in onto the things that you need to key on. And um it's been it's been dope to see, honestly, just how he would been able to come in and get all the guys on the same page so fast. And I feel like they've been executing fairly well, and there's been a lot of back and forth with uh us going against them and things like that. So, it's been pretty good. >> A closer look at all that eye candy coming soon enough as we get closer to training camp. And we'll get to see that with some healthy players who are still recovering from injuries from last year. >> Mini camp is the last time we'll see all the guys share the field together until training camp when the guys report to State Farm Stadium on July 22nd. They'll begin the off-season program getting ready for the regular season a little bit earlier because they're set to play in the Hall of Fame game against the Carolina Panthers days before Larry Fitzgerald is enshrined to the Hall. >> Still ahead, the Cardinals continue making an impact in the community as team owner Michael Bidwill treats Arizona students to a trip of a lifetime. You're watching Cardinals Bird Watch presented by SeatGeek. Cardinals Bird Watch is sponsored by State Farm. Like a good neighbor, State Farm is there. >> Picture this. An all-expenses-paid trip, three days, four nights in our nation's capital. Fly on the Cardinals' private team plane, get a private tour of the Supreme Court, and get to see the most impressive museums and monuments this country has to offer. >> Picture this, Danny. We lived it. We took part in the annual Civics Matters Arizona trip just a few years ago. But this year, it was the fifth annual trip. Nearly 280 different students from 55 different schools all throughout the state had that opportunity to take part in that partnership with the close-up foundation and Governor Hobbs' office for what turned out to be a life-changing experience. >> A program cultivating civic education and responsible citizenship for young students who are shaping our future. Here's a look at their send-off to Washington, D.C. as part of a once-in-a-lifetime experience. >> So, we are getting ready to leave for the Civics Matters trip. That's especially true for our younger generation like each of you here today. >> I'm passionate about civics because I feel like it is an under-discussed subject and I feel like it does need more recognition. I am so excited to be able to have this opportunity and to go on the Cardinals plane. I am so excited because it's going to be such a unique experience. >> Zack, you and I have both had the pleasure of going on this trip. For many students, it's their first time on a plane. Getting to see their curiosity and passion behind learning about our nation's history and how they can shape its future is really special. >> As much as this experience is about what you learn in D.C., it's also about what you do after that. And you heard a little bit from Abigail Hurst, a high school senior who is set to enroll at the Naval Academy. She had some interest in civics prior to the trip, but then after the trip, she felt inspired and felt that she needed to do more, and that is why she's on her way to becoming a midshipman. Coming up, >> Danny and Zach break down what coaches had to say as mini camp got underway. More Cardinals bird watch after the [music] break. The segment is presented by SeatGeek, official primary ticketing partner of the Arizona Cardinals. >> As we enter the true off season where players and coaches are away from the building for roughly 6 weeks, we have to savor every last bit of football that we have. Zach, this week it was mandatory workouts, mini camp with big changes. At least that's what we've been told with the defense. >> Look, every year coaches are going to make changes. The fundamentals and the foundations and principles of your ideology are always going to remain the same. In the case of Nick Rallis, it will always be motor and violence. But still, the defensive coordinator was forthcoming with us, Danny, when we talked with him, and he realized changes needed to be made on a little bit of a bigger level, and that's what we're starting to see throughout this off season. >> At the end of the day, like, no matter what we're doing schematically, how do we get the players to be in the best spot where they're playing at their best and they can go out there and win the game, you know? And so that was ultimately like the underlying thing is like, are the players going to be really good at executing this? And if not, like, throw it out. So, um it's so layered, so many variables to this game, and you're not going to be able to say, "Oh, yep, I have the answer right there." But you better be ready to adapt, and you better be ready to continue adapt as, you know, we go through OTAs and training camp and the >> Changes were needed, and changes have been made. A league-wide change in recent years, quarterback development time. Gone are the days of giving a QB 3 to 4 years to develop. The NFL runs on urgency. That can be a tough balance when you have these young quarterbacks who are adjusting to new coverages and the speed of the game compared to what they saw in college. >> Mike LaFleur acknowledged that when it comes to that rookie class, yeah, you have to be patient with them, but there still is that urgency if you are that rookie to make sure you are ready. In the case of offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett, who Danny, we both know has been around football for quite a bit of time, he told us you treat every quarterback the exact same. But in the case of Carson Beck, the rookie that the Cardinals drafted in the third round, you don't want to rush that process to making sure he's ready. >> Right now, um we just have to keep pushing him and keep pushing him. And you want young guys to stay out as long as they possibly can just learn. I mean, just even the process through a week, the process through a season. Yeah, I mean, it's a marathon through the uh training camp, preseason games, the 17-game The speed of the game, we mentioned I mentioned that before. I mean, it's it's like nothing else. And there's so many things that go through a quarterback's mind um from just what hash, why the call, what are the statistics, am I throwing right, am I throwing left, where's one, what do I do with the protection? I mean, I can go on and on with everything that they have to think about. >> That rookie learning curve applied to running back Jeremiah Love as well, who was seen returning kicks during OTAs. Zach, that's sparked a bit of a discussion online given his expected workload as the third overall pick. >> And the special teams coordinator Michael Goberial, he not sure if he heard about it, but he definitely put that rumor to rest because he said this time of the year, you're just testing out all these different possibilities. >> If the opportunity presents itself to where he can take care of the football back there, um and we're keeping the volume of snaps depending on what he does offensively, you know, it's something we'll certainly work out. So, right now in the offseason, we usually train everybody to do these things cuz you never know in the game whether there's an injury or not. Um if a guy has to come out in the game in the second half and be able to help you, but he just certainly has a run skill to be able to do it. >> Goberial is asking his unit to play hard at all times since they don't have four downs to make a play. That means they don't get to pick and choose when they're playing hard or physical. >> It's that stubborn refusal that coach Goby talked about because he said you cannot let the guy that you're guarding get by you because on special teams you have the opportunity to swing the momentum in your direction. >> Still ahead, Zach Gershman breaks down why a healthy Marvin Harrison Jr. could be poised for a breakout season. Cardinals Bird Watch continues in a moment presented by SeatGeek. This segment is sponsored by Desert Financial Credit Union, official banking partner of the Arizona Cardinals. >> Hey, hey everybody and welcome in to Inside Voices. Cardinals insider Zach Gershman. We spoke with wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. for the first time since the 2025 season came to a close. A year that featured quite a few more downs than they did ups. And for the first time in Harrison Jr.'s football life, injuries were a part of the conversation. He had that concussion in week six, the appendicitis surgery after week 10, and two separate foot injuries that had the wide receiver sidelined. Point-blank, he wasn't thrilled. >> Turn it up. >> Yeah, I mean it sucks not playing. Um I've never not played. I've never kind of been injured, never missed a game. >> From little league to high school to college to so staying on the sideline, I mean it definitely sucked um you know for almost half the year basically, so I think not only set a light of fire, it just one makes you appreciate the game more. I'm concerned about what Marvin looks like right now. And did he improve from yesterday? And I would say yeah, but I mean you mean, not that you know, everyone's going to see the tape from today. Thought he Thought he made a stride today. It's awesome. Like a lot Like I thought a lot of guys did. And there are other guys that might have had a better day yesterday. Now, let's go improve and see how we can correct those mistakes. So, again, just focused on the on the day-to-day with him and and keeping him and all these guys just where their feet are in the present, not worrying about, you know, come September and all those other games after. >> Everyone on social media will have their comments about Harrison and his performance over the course of his first two seasons in the NFL. And by all means, he wants to, you know, be his dad in every single way. Not just cuz he's a son, but because this is his own career. You know, so right now he's starting to He's in a mode right now where he wants to fight for everything that he wants to achieve. And right now he's not looking at the past couple years. He's looking at how can he fight to get what he wants right now. Then this time next year, how can he fight to get it again? You know, even if he's done everything everyone here wants to see, again, you have to fight to do it again. You can't just do it one time and just start to sit back and to reminisce on that too much, you know what I mean? So, he's just He's just a fighter right now, keeping his head on. He's still just as quiet, but he's smiling. Um just cuz he's dialed in and he's focused. You know, cuz you know, he knows why he's here. He knows what the fans want to see. He knows what, you know, the team knows he can do. And I've seen him do it since he was like 18. >> Marvin's a stud. He's a guy who's probably one of the hardest workers I've seen. A guy who does everything the right way. And yeah, he got a little, you know, banged up last year. And that's a bummer. Just with his, you know, injury history, he's never really been hurt. So, I'm excited to, you know, have him back, get him back on the field, cuz when he's on the field, defenses have to be aware of where he's at and what he's doing, cuz he's a guy who can wreck a game and and he's a huge asset for us. So, um we would love to have him back at full going. Uh you know, obviously he's still getting back whatever he's doing, but he's a he's had a great, you know, OTAs and I'm excited to see him continue to grow. >> With Lafluer in the building, much of this off-season program has been spent learning the offense. That's the fun part for Marvin Harrison and his teammates, but that fun can reach new heights if health is on Harrison's side. >> Coming up, Danny and Zach break down and react to the latest headlines surrounding the team. Cardinals Bird Watch continues after this, presented by SeatGeek. Welcome back to Cardinals Bird Watch, presented by SeatGeek. This segment is presented by AMPM. >> Welcome back in to Cardinals Bird Watch time for read and react. Now that mini camp has come and gone and the players and coaches are gone for a bit of a break, Zach, what constitutes a successful off-season program? >> I think it's just learning those installs, getting the playbook down pat, especially with a new first-year head coach. But I think Michael Lafluer canceling that final day of mini camp was a good sign for this team that they're moving in the right direction. >> What constitutes a successful off-season program? Staying healthy, which is something Lafluer confirmed that this team is. You don't want to be banged up going into training camp, more so than players already are recovering from the previous year. The fact that this is a new coaching staff, you also want to make sure that the players are on the right track and understanding the playbook, and are they already able to have up-speed, high-tempo practices, which from what we've seen, the answer to that is yes. Reaction for this one for you, quarterback Gardner Minshew was the biggest winner of this off-season. >> 100% I believe so. With Jacoby Brissett trying to figure out his contract situation, reportedly, it gave Gardner Minshew the opportunity to earn some of those QB1 snaps. We know from his previous stops in Philadelphia, he sat behind Jalen Hurts. He wasn't going to beat out Jalen Hurts. And then last year in Kansas City, it's with Patrick Mahomes who reportedly also just inked a major contract. So now that he is here with Jacoby Brissett trying to figure out his situation, he had the opportunity to earn those QB1 snaps. >> Reps are golden. They are irreplaceable. And the fact that Gardner Minshew was able to get those so early on in a new spot with him and a new coaching staff, new teammates, that is something that cannot be replicated elsewhere. Building chemistry with his teammates as well as the play callers and understanding what could be asked of him if Gardner Minshew was asked to play. Well, we heard from the head coach Mike LaFleur about the sky being the limit for tight end Trey McBride. How much more can number 85 truly show us, Zach? >> I don't know, but if whatever it is, it's going to be impressive. For him to put up the over 1,200 yards like he did last year to set the NFL record for a tight end with receptions with 126, it's going to be very tough to top that, especially when you look at all the weapons that are going to be out there in a healthy Marvin Harrison Jr. returning. But Trey McBride has proven time and time again he's the player that's able to do it. >> It's about consistency. That's something McBride has shown us throughout his career regardless of how many snaps he's getting, regardless of who is throwing him the football. Just being consistent with what we've seen in terms of his catchability, running through defenders, being a full complete tight end with his blocking ability. We know that he can put up those numbers. It's just about doing that consistently. Zach, I know you love football. What about football? It is World Cup time. Are you watching? >> So if you asked me about a year ago, I could really care less. But whenever the World Cup comes around, that's always when I put on my USMNT hat and I get ready to talk about how amazing American soccer is compared to the rest of the world. But this year, I'm not so sure. I'm not so sure. I'm excited to see it in all the different stadiums, especially a lot of those NFL venues. But I don't know. We'll see. We'll see how much I watch. >> I feel like you'll change your mind. Once you see everyone around you and everyone online is talking about the World Cup, you'll probably be sucked right in. >> I It's the patriot in me. I hope so. >> Absolutely. I'm excited. First of all, I grew up playing soccer. I enjoy watching soccer. But the World Cup is so fun just because you have people from all around the world coming together and you have everybody coming together online. >> I think my time playing soccer when I was like 7, 8 years old. This is when I start to showcase that knowledge in case I need to start flexing on some people. >> Well, on that note, we will wrap it up for Cardinals Bird Watch this week. We'll be here next week, same time, same place. For Zach Gershman, I'm Dani Soria. Thanks so much for tuning in. >> Thank you for watching Cardinals Bird Watch presented by SeatGeek.

Um obviously I want to get in the offense as well. Um but I'm here to play. Um, I just need the opportunity. Um, and I'm pa- I'm patiently waiting and and that time and that time will come. Um, and if and when that time comes, I'll be ready for the opportunity. >> What made this an attractive opportunity for you? >> It's home. >> Yeah, so it's not the biggest >> It's It's It's home. Um, my my parents are here. I get to see my family. Uh, I definitely originally had like some complications being with my family, too. So, just being here, uh, just being able to be home with my family and I know some of some most of these guys in the building, too. Um, so it was just just the reality of being home and being close to my family. Um, and then the love of the game as well. Uh, just playing football at home is it couldn't be no better opportunity. Yes, sir. >> I got you. >> Yeah, no doubt. No doubt. >> Have you gotten a chance to bond with some of the other guys who are from the area like Corey Levin, Tyler or sorry, you are Tyler Davidson. Keelan Marion, have you gotten to bond with any of those guys? >> Yes, sir. Yes, sir, for sure. Uh, especially uh, me and Keelan, uh, cuz we played in high school a little bit uh, against each other, him going to uh, Grayson or what not. Uh, so we talk about that stuff all the time and we all just talk about uh, the games we played against each other, uh, what we did like we trained together and stuff like that. So, like this just this whole OTA period has been like a a memory lane trip for me, you know. >> Has being from the area given you kind of an advantage when it comes to bonding with some of your new teammates? >> Uh, yes, definitely cuz um, when you tend to leave another team it's and go to another team it's tend to figure out how people in the building move, uh, figure out who your teammates are and um, and how your and how your teammates are going to act towards you. For me it was I was already comfortable cuz I knew some of the guys in here, um, which makes it more comfortable for you cuz you're able to be more social and then able to be more relaxed. So, uh, that was definitely key for me. >> What was your first reaction when you heard about the news? >> Uh, I mean, honestly, bro, I was on the golf course. Uh, and I I mean, up to that point I had not, uh, had I hadn't had any um conversation after the last conversation I had with them. Uh and to me uh from what I knew it was kind of copacetic like um on still being there. Uh so when I did get the news it was a shock, but it was a good shock, you know what I'm saying knowing the opportunity that I had here. Um and knowing the opportunity I still have here, so. >> How how is the opportunity different for >> Uh you know, in Jacksonville uh the starting three technique is that I can only stay in there and they pay him X amount of dollars a year. Um so here I have an opportunity to have more of a feature role in the defense um whereas really it just kind of going in the game to get somebody out the game if you feel that in any sense. For sure. >> So that run defense has been a big talking point about like what you bring to this defensive line. You know, how would you assess your own kind of qualities and what you bring to the group? >> Um I I think I'm more than just a run run stopper to be honest. I feel like I can rush a lot more. Um just having to learn uh you know, my my three years in college and then my first two years in the league run the run game was kind of something that I had to get better at and um just grow in that in that area. And here man, we the scheme that we play here is different than what I've been playing. Uh but I feel like this scheme is definitely built for a guy like me, fast feet um and just be able to make plays with athleticism. >> Yeah, I mean it feels very sounds bad like one note, but just like go go ahead and go fast as possible. >> and I mean that's I hadn't played like that since high school, bro. So I mean I'm excited. I'm excited. And I think I think it'll be a lot better run game defense will be a lot better this year. Um I feel like we'll be a lot well rounded. >> Need all these senses like running like a the lights off or are they running >> In a dark room. >> In a dark room, right? So like how does that kind of fit what you do? Like you said you haven't done it since high school, so it's it's like riding a bike. >> Um no, I mean it's just playing fast, but it's the other techniques in football of defensive line play. I feel like to a certain extent it takes some type of thinking. In this defense, no thinking. Go. See, you kind of do what you see fit. I mean, there's definitely rules that you got to follow, but you know, Coach Ali is the first coach that um you know, never really not I don't want to say not correcting me on certain things, but like he's more worried about you know, us getting off the ball, us disrupting the play, whereas um where I had my hands or something like that, little stuff. Um he really just wants us to get off the ball and get vertical and you know, play how we play. So, I mean, I think it's going to be a great um for myself and not only for myself, but for the other guys. >> You said you you want to be viewed as more than just a run stopper. >> For sure. >> What are you would you say as a as a pass rusher, somebody you can kind of elevate in that way? >> Um yeah, for sure. Uh last year, to be honest, was my worst year pass rushing or on paper. Um you know, if you look at the film, I still was winning. It's just that you know, things happen. Um and you're not always going to get the sack, but you know, just putting it all together. Um I want to be a complete player. I don't want to be known as one thing or the other thing. Um and just continuing to grow my bag and shoot, continuing to get better, man. >> How do you feel like your first going in the sport? >> Uh I'd say it's been rocky, up and down. Um but at the end of day, you know, I've stuck it out the long run. A lot of guys that have been through what I've been through in the first 2 years of the league, you know, it could it might be uh you know, something that could knock their confidence or something like that, and I'm always going to believe in myself, regardless on if I got traded, you know, in April or not. I already knew what I was going to do this year, and that's still the plan. And you know what I'm saying? That That's always been the plan. I've been working since 2 weeks after we got done in the playoffs or they got done in the playoffs. So, you know, regardless on if I was here, if I was there, if I was anywhere, um I already had that on my mind. Uh you know, my rookie year wasn't bad at all. I uh I finished the year pretty good. So, you know, going into that off season, I didn't really have a bad taste in my mouth. In this past year, you know what I'm Personally for me, I feel like it was the worst year of football um for myself, for my career, since you know, since forever. Um so, you know, having that bad taste in your mouth, it make you work a little harder, it make you do little things do things a little different, it make you look at things different. So, that's the approach I've been taking this off season, and that's the approach I took before the trade, after the trade, and that's the approach I'm going to take for the rest. >> And now you feel really like you're done, and you're in a place that really wants you? >> Hell yeah. You You rather be somewhere that you celebrated, not tolerated, bro. At the end of the day, um so, I'm here for a reason. God put me here for a reason. I'm ready to go ball. >> Talk about the possibilities for this defense. >> Um I think the possibilities are endless. I think um through the draft and through the guys who we got in free agency, um I think you got a lot of pieces. Now, I feel like it might be a little hard to find out where you going to put all the pieces, but at least you got them. You know what I'm saying? Uh so, that's good. That's good problems to have, but I I think the possibilities are endless. I think the linebacker core is stronger. I think the DB room is strong, and I think we strong, too. And you know, I feel like a lot Coach Nagy always say, you know, people sleeping on us, and we like that, though. We like that adversity. We like people not really, you know, cuz if they count you out, it's going to hit you it's going to hit them it's going to hit them a little harder when you knock them out. So, you know, I I feel like we ready for it. We ready for everything that come with it, so. >> You You had mentioned that when you got there, your habits weren't very good. >> Um >> remember that? >> Uh yeah. I I can say as far as like uh just taking coaching wise, I say I came a long way. Uh that was probably my biggest one right there, just >> So, then after that, you went to Western Illinois? >> Western Illinois. I missed a whole year of football after that. I uh where I got in a situation on field uh with another player, ended up having to miss uh, basically the whole year of football. Got a job, was working. Then after that, that's when I went to Iowa Western. >> A job? >> Yeah, a job. >> What job was it? >> working at Honda back at home. Doing like stickers and stuff, taking it out, cleaning the cars. >> Was it fun? Did you enjoy it? >> I wouldn't say I enjoyed it, but I just had to reality life, you know? So. >> What was the hardest part about that year off? >> Uh, just not playing, you know? Not being able to take some stuff out on the field. Uh, stuff like that, man. You miss it the most, but uh, I just the journey I've been in, I I wouldn't change it for nothing. Uh, think it was all worth it at the end, so. >> How much did that year away kind of like change you on field as a player? >> Changed a lot. Uh, really basically something I thought it was all over with uh, at one point, but uh, just the right people in my life and uh, just like that, just stay with it, stay getting my uh, school work done and just working. >> What's been your >> on Go ahead, Dan. >> In that time period, who'd you kind of lean on the most? >> Uh, I really say my my uncle Dan, uh, not really having my dad, you know, my dad was locked up, so. But my uncle was like I'll say a father figure to me. So uh, he looked out a lot for me, so. Just that and my family, so. >> And then how how did you rejoin after that that time off? Like how did how how did that unfold of like reaching out to the staff and say, "Hey, can I come back?" Or or how did it >> No, actually uh, Western Illinois, they reached out, uh, came to my house, uh, talked to me and they were still interested in me, so. Ended up just working out, so. >> What's been your secret to sticking around here? >> I say what secret? um, my bad. >> No, that's quest all right. >> Maybe secret is the wrong word. What's the Why have you been able to stick around here? What have you done well? >> I think the most most thing I just did change the way I work and just trying to be consistent in everything I do. I mean, I'm a undrafted free agent not supposed to last long if you want to say, but you always just got to work, so. >> How much have you grown and developed since since you first came to this team? Have you like developed new skills? Have you improved like >> I say I've improved a lot overall, but when I say what changed playing in the XFL then coming here kind of helped me a lot and just staying on top of things like say like even with talking to coach just staying consistent. That was that was probably my biggest thing, you know, and I think if I just stay consistent in everything I do weight room, nutrition and stuff like that I think I'll be pretty good, so. >> Is that kind of what you learned in the XFL? Like did it like open your eyes to you okay, I need to do this or >> I'd say being in XFL, you know, from being in the league I haven't played I didn't play for about 3 years. So, when I got to the XFL I played a lot of snaps, so. Just getting back into it and getting it back and loving the game again in that >> What do you like about the makeup of this team when you think about the leadership, the guys that you guys have here now? What would you say is kind of a difference since you've been here last couple of years? >> I'd say far as like just I think you got a lot of leaders on the team and a lot of people that's come ready to work and not too much complaining I'd say. >> What have you what have you seen from DeShawn so far? >> DeShawn he's a leader speak up about a lot of things you know, you can talk to him about anything he's seen a lot of stuff you know, as a friend any of teammate whatever you want to do and DeShawn's that type of guy he just you talk to him about anything work hard stuff like that, so.

title: Michael Penix Jr. on Atlanta Falcons mandatory minicamp & excitement for season
text: Healthwise, u I'm right where I need to be. Um, still making strides dayto day. Um, not 100% yet, but you know, I know I will be, you know, right on time. So, >> week one's always kind of been the plan for you, right? Is that still online on track for that? >> Yeah, absolutely, man. We just working, you know, trying to try to take it one day at a time and just control what I can control now. And, you know, that's just making sure I'm doing everything I can to make sure my body is ready for that for a week one game. So, >> what is the uh the next milestone like the next goal for you? the next milestone. Uh for me, um taking contact, you know, because right now it's everything's non-cont and you know that's tough, you know, obviously with quarterbacks, we don't get we don't get touch in practice, you know. Um so my first contact like we can do simulation drills and stuff like that, but you know, but obviously, you know, for all the quarterbacks across the league, the first time you get hit is your first game uh of the season. So, um, but that that'll be the next next step, you know, just making sure I'm confident in in my knee and confident to be able to take contact and keep playing. So, >> it's not doing 11 on 111. Is that just so nobody? >> Yeah. >> Yeah. Just, you know, just precaution. >> When when it comes to everything, even beyond injuries, how far away are you from being the type of NFL quarterback that you want to be? >> Yeah, I mean, man, I don't, like I said, I just take it one day at a time. you know, each and every day I'm trying to get better. You know, doing whatever I can to help this team with football games. That's that's the ultimate goal. So, you know, for me, I'm not looking in the long run is like, oh, this is where, you know, this is the line to be this type of quarterback. You know, I'm I just want to, you know, whatever whatever things I have in my head and, you know, down on paper to that I want to accomplish each and every day. That's what I'm doing. I'm taking it day by day so that I can you know get to you know whatever level that is that um um whoever want to you know whatever picture that people want to paint you know. >> Yeah. And and also mentally I mean you've had a lot of injuries obviously. Is it easier mentally to recover from an injury now compared to what it was say in Indiana? >> I wouldn't say it's easier. Uh I feel like you have a better understanding you know of of your body. you you have a better understanding of, you know, where you're at in your rehab process and stuff like that, you know, but it it's nothing nothing about it is easy. You know, it's tough not being a being able to be out there and do do the thing you love to do. So, I wouldn't say anything is is easier, but you know, you do have a better understanding of your body and you you know, you know, when to push yourself and when to, you know, cut back and be like, "All right, I need I need some time." So, >> do you expect to be ready for 111 cleared by training camp? >> Yeah, that's Yeah, that's the expectation. you know, I know I go see my doctor before um all that all that kicks off. So, you know, it's it's really up to my doctor. >> Mike, we see they put you through a bunch of different well all the QB through a lot of drills. Uh has anything surprised you when you went through like, oh, okay, I feel good doing this as opposed to like I was a little cautious thinking what can I do? >> Um no, I mean I felt confident with everything. It's sometimes they they say drills, they tell the trainers, they stand to the side and tell me no, you can't do it. And I'm like I feel like I can do it. But, you know, but I I just, you know, listen to those guys and, you know, just um like I said, continue to just trust my body, trust that trust my knee, and um you know, if it was up to me, I go out there and do everything. I'll do 110 on 111 now, you know, but like that's and obviously, you know, the smart thing, you know, just understanding, you know, it's it's more than just, you know, just my want to play, you know, it obviously I got to care about my body and, you know, my future as well. So >> I remember tearing my ACL there were certain parts throughout the process that you enjoyed and have you reached some of those points in the process you like okay I'm taking that next step in the process of getting better and getting ready as how I was >> Yeah absolutely um I feel like I reach it every day you know um you know just the just the way that I feel during drills like from day one to how I feel now doing every drill it's like it I feel those differences so I would say just it's not is just one specific thing, you know, it's everything that I'm doing. Like each and every day I come out here, I feel better than the day before. So like I feel like that's a good thing. >> Mike, you clearly have like some you're raring to go a little bit. Where do you channel kind of that energy you have if you're unable to do that out in 111? Like is it extra film work? Is it extra time in the recovery, you know, like process? >> Yeah, I mean that's Yeah, that's mandatory, you know, just the recovery process, you know, just um you know, trusting in it, you know. Um, you know, I work with Nick and he he push he pushes me every day. And some days, you know, I we kind of like butttheads, but I know he he wants the best for me. And um, you know, sometimes I want to do more, sometimes I don't want to do as much, you know, but we have those days, but um, you know, like I said, just trusting in the process and just staying where my feet are, you know, that's what it's about. >> And how are you feeling comfortwise with the scheme and and kind of the new offenses here? >> Yeah, I love it. It's been great. It's been great so far. I feel like the whole team has been adjusting very well and you know the offense is looking really good. So >> we were talking to ABP last week and it seems like him and Stfansky are all about the footwork when it comes to quarterbacks. So what what is different for you I guess with this like you know with how they're coaching now? >> Um I would say just like you said like just the amount of time put into it, you know. Uh I feel like it's just a lot of time put into it. It's always something that's getting pointed out, you know, in routes on there if if you're off time and it's always like, hey, they're let letting you know, hey, you got to quicken up your feet or, you know, take your time a little bit on this drop. You got to work through your progression. Like just stuff like that. So, I feel like it's just something that is talked about more um than than it was. So, >> Mike, the movement part of it is a big part of the game, too. And I saw there was a couple instances where you had to get out and had the scramble drum going. How were you mentally with that part of the game when all right, you got a quick reaction. you got to move and go. >> Uh, I don't think about it. That's the thing. I don't think about it. And uh, you know, I know I can't. They they the trainers don't want me like flipping my hips like as I'm running. You know what I'm saying? Like, so it's sometimes I I have to I have to know like I I understand what I can do and what I can't do. But sometimes I get out the pocket and I I'm like, "Oh, I want to run, but I'm like, "All right, I ain't supposed to be doing all that." So, um, but, uh, I'm just playing the game. Just playing the game. you know, if I if I don't have a read, I can't just sit there and p in the pocket and take a sack. You know, I just try to get out and do what I can. But obviously, you know, just being smart with it. >> When it comes to footwork stuff, is it is it kind of just reinforcing stuff that you already knew or is it kind of new wrinkles to what you already knew? >> Uh, it's reinforcing things I've already known. Um, yeah, I would say, yeah, just reinforcing. Is part of it having to work with some of these new receivers that you've got to Zachariah Branch, John Dodson, make sure the timing is is right with those guys and the footwork. >> Um, >> yeah. Yeah, absolutely. Yeah, for sure. Um, I know like it's it's different. You know, when you got, you know, you got man, it's man coverage. You know, you looking at you looking at your matchups and stuff. You got to that's when you really got to dial into knowing your guys. You know, when you got zones, I'm like, "All right, if I got a three-step implant throw, you know, I'm putting it to a spot. I'm expecting you to be there, you know. So, it's it's kind of both of those things. So, >> Tua has been pretty uh complimentary toward you, you know, at least at least with us. Um what is that relationship like? How has that developed with you guys? >> Yeah, it's been good. You know, it's been nothing but good since he got here. You know, we know we in competition, but at the same time, you know, we we on the same team and we we we got the same goals and that's to see this team win football games and, you know, help help do that in our way. So, um, man, we we've been we've been good together, and you know, it's always going to be like that. So,

title: Atlanta Falcons Head Coach Kevin Stefanski discusses Mandatory Minicamp and team development
text: Heat. Heat. Hey, hey, hey. Heat. Okay, mandatory mini camp. Excited to get going with the guys this week. We'll have a practice today, a walk through this afternoon, practice tomorrow, uh morning. Um we'll have some mandatory meetings from the league that we'll knock out uh in this mini camp and then we'll we'll take a a break here. But really pleased with the work that the guys have put into this uh you know and and it's an all-encompassing type of work. It's what they've done in the meeting rooms, what they've done in the weight room, what they've done on the grass. Uh really a group that works. So, uh, these next two days and this mini camp are really important, uh, really an important part of our offseason program. We want to make sure that we, you know, finish strong and everything we're doing, but, uh, excited about the next couple days out there on the grass. And with that, I'll take any questions. >> Is James Pierce Jr. here with you guys? >> Yes. >> And what is that decision to have him back? >> Yeah, I think throughout this uh throughout every uh situation, you take in all the information available to you. Uh obviously uh this being our mandatory portion of our um program. Uh he will do work in the weight room. He'll do individual he's not going to do team settings, team period type stuff yet. Uh I just feel like with him not being here for the offseason program to date. I don't think it's fair to put him in those type of drills, but uh he'll be out there. >> How do you handle trying to like reintegrate him within a locker room? >> Yeah, I I think uh you know those type of things are football teams and and locker rooms and and those are organic things and I believe in the people that we have in our locker room and and you know I think any player that comes into our building uh understands what's expected of that player and and uh you know understands what's important to this football team. >> You view it as a relief to have him here now and not have to wait until like late July to have him around here. You know, I'm so focused on I got the blinders on. So, I really I can't speak to the past the, you know, what's in the future. Just I'm excited that everybody's here uh ready to work. >> What have your conversations been like with James so far? >> U you know, I'm not going to get into specifics about conversations really with any player. You know, I like to keep those private. Uh but he he understands what's expected of him. Have there been has there been any word from the NFL or league office regarding any suspensions or anything like that at this point? >> No. [snorts] When >> you say he understands what's expected of him, what is expected of them? What do you mean by that? >> Yeah, I think again don't want to get into specifics of the conversations that we have, but uh all of our players uh are understand what they need to do both in and out of this building. In your experience, coach, what is it you look for for a player who's been not a part of of the workouts and now joining in? What are some things that you watch for? >> I think every situation's different and and u you want to make sure that your players are as as they're introduced to your um schemes and and to your program that they understand why you're doing what you're doing. I should also mention we'll have some guys out there that are on a here on a trial basis the next couple days. So, uh, everybody's in a different place, if you will, and just making sure that they're understanding why you're doing what you're doing. >> Is Michael Penser cleared for 11 on 111? >> Uh, he's not cleared for 11 on 111. So, we'll we'll continue with the plan uh with what Mike has done to date. Very pleased with with the work that he's putting in. Uh, he's ex like I mentioned to you guys, I think before, he's exactly where he needs to be. Um, we'll just continue to lean on uh medical and and Mike and continue to make good decisions uh for his rehabilitation. >> How hard is it to kind of hold him back? Because I'd imagine he really wants to be 100 just really roll. I mean, how hard is it to kind of hold him a little bit? >> You know, it's a good question. And I think for any player, it's our job uh often times to protect the player from the player. And and uh I have to, you know, I'm not a medical expert, so I lean on our experts and I I take their lead in terms of what any player rehabbing is able to do. And uh it's not our job as coaches to tell uh the medical team what a player should do. So in this case, very very comfortable with the the the plan that we have. Um and and keeping Mike uh a breast of all those decisions and and where he is very very similar to how you do it with all your players, making sure they understand uh where they are in their rehab, what they're able to do, uh how we're going to transition into different phases, if you will. Uh so very comfortable with where we are. >> I believe mentioned Gohead. Go ahead. >> Yeah. I believe last week Alex had mentioned the QB race can't really start until Mike is healthy, entirely healthy. How how much of an issue is that? I mean, have you guys kind of lost an a time period here where you would like to have him? >> Yeah, we're we're not giving out any jobs in June. Uh so, uh we'll continue with every player at every position to uh bring the guys along at the pace that they're able to. So, obviously with Mike, he's rehabbing from an injury. Uh he's, you know, been able to do seven on seven, do individual with us, which he's attacking and doing a great job with. uh with any competition, quote unquote, uh those things work themselves out down the line. Uh but but we just have to be uh as a uh team, I I think we have to realize, players have to realize that we're all working towards the same goal right now in June, and that's building a foundation for this football season. >> You haven't seen Antario Thompson yet. Is that injury related or is there something else? >> Injury related, but he's working through it. A lot of conver coach a lot of conversation was talked about uh Mike under center and uh we've seen him do a lot of different stuff. Have you seen him evolve? >> How about you DJ? Were you under center at all? >> Sometimes [laughter] you're not, man. Yeah, it's a it's it's a interesting uh the league goes through waves and and trends and uh you know I remember back at 2006 guys teams were under center on third and 11 and the game has changed just the usage of motion uh the usage of subde defense there's just so many things that the game continues to change and there's es and flows to it and shotgun certainly continues to go up and and there's great reasons for it. Then there's also, you know, great reasons to put a quarterback under center and uh as they play young players come out of the high school game, come out of the the college game, uh there there sometimes is a effort to get guys comfortable taking a snap from under center, dropping from under center, taking a sevenstep drop from under center. There's there's a lot of nuance that goes with that. Uh so I've just seen it in my time the evolution of of getting back under center uh because there's uh there's some benefits to it both in the run game and the pass game. So there's also a piece of this where we have to uh for guys that haven't had a ton of su not success a ton of experience doing that you got to bring them along and you get back to the basics. But uh it's it's something that I I think has its benefits for certain run schemes for certain pass schemes. Uh but it doesn't mean that shotgun is going away. >> Will we see Kendall Daniels during mandatory camp >> practicing? >> Uh he will not practice just yet. Yeah. Still rehabbing >> with Mike. You talked about the being part of his rehab to get back on the field. Has he been able to do more from when OTAA started to to where he is now? >> I think it's it's a volume thing that that you're constantly uh increasing. Uh there there's as part of this is an act of rehab. Uh taking the individual drills that he's done. Uh those individual drills aren't easy and a lot of what we do whether it's going over bags or or whatever it may be. Coach Van Pelt puts those guys through paces. So he's done a great job with with everything that we've thrown at him. Obviously there's limitations with the the 11 on 111. Uh but very very comfortable with the work that he's gotten in to date. Is there an expectation that by the time training camp starts he will be a full participant? >> Uh I think we'll get to training camp. We we'll have those type of discussions. Obviously as a medical team uh we have a plan in place, but you also have to go off of the player and and the milestones that the player's hitting before you can really make those final determinations. >> Coach, you turn your ACL when you >> How hard is it for you to see all these players go back through and what? >> Well, that was a non-athlete tearing his ACL. These guys are These guys are athletes. >> Well, I mean, you were kind of highly regarded when you came out of high school. What do you think it is now that is different for getting people back on the field that maybe it wasn't when you were playing? >> So, I'm going to tell a quick story. So, um, I tore my ACL my sophomore year, I think, and, uh, my brothers, God love them, they sent a video to my sons of of me laying on the ground after tearing my ACL, you know, diabolical. And, uh, my son uh sent me a screenshot of me laying on the ground and he wrote back, "Are you hurt or are you injured?" [laughter] And I wrote back, I said, "Both." Um, so anyway, uh, yeah, that the ACL tears, you hear stories about athletes from the 70s and and the the invasive nature of those surgeries and my god, the medical uh, community and and what we've been able to do over the course of time has been incredible. So, uh I I can only tell you from uh my experience, um those are tough injuries and and you hear some of the guys like the the what you have to go through when you're pushing yourself through those injuries in in in order to get back. So, I marvel both medically what we're able to do these days. And I marvel at how our guys push themselves through this. And uh it's it's truly incredible to see a guy uh whether we're talking about Mike or anybody pushing through some of these major injuries when they work in tandem with a medical group that we have here who are outstanding and they put so much effort into it, how quickly they're able to get back and how quickly they're able to regain their strength. And u not to say that we're not going to be smart about all of our rehab with our players, but uh it it's pretty impressive to watch how these guys come back. And you know, I think the other point of this is there's not a camera following them around all the time. So, a lot of times we as fans just see the end result and what you don't see is my god, the amount of work that that went into it. So, uh I'm really impressed with with all our of our guys that are pushing through these injuries and uh you know, luckily they're they're better athletes than I am. >> Do you think it's harder for quarterbacks than any other position? >> I wouldn't I wouldn't characterize it that way. No. Uh I think you know every position has different movement skills that for that uh that you know are required of the position and think about an offensive lineman or a defensive lineman coming out of a three-point stance and the explosion that they have to have maybe is a little bit different than a wide receiver coming out of a two-point stance and some of the change of direction of a DB or a wide receiver a little bit different than one of the guys in in the trenches so to speak. So, uh, it's I I wouldn't say one's harder than the other. I just think they're again, uh, incredible to for me to witness. I I, you know, I get the front row seat to watch these guys every day at the work that they put into it. Um, but I'm I'm really pleased with with how these guys are attacking their rehabs. >> Thank you, >> coach. What do you enjoy most about your first off season with this uh team right here? >> Yeah, it's a team that works. uh you know, you watch the the best players in this football team work the hardest and and uh they push each other and that that's been impressive for me to watch. Again, there's been a thousand meetings, I think over 12 hours of team meetings, over 12 hours of offense, defense meetings. I tallied it up. Uh there's been a lot thrown at them and the guys have have attacked it and they've pushed each other and and I appreciate that. I get to sit back and observe how a team works in the weight room just watching just you know watching and and seeing how they push and you know there's there's something to be said when when you're got that amount of weight on your back or you're pushing that that bar. I mean it's it's it's hard and and I can appreciate watching these guys do it and watching them push themselves on the grass here. It's a it's it's a group that uh is not shy about the work that is required. uh at right tackle. How does losing storm kind of impact what you're doing there? And then also just on Jawan uh kind of if you can detail at all what he's been dealing with, why he hasn't been able >> Sure. He he's rehabbing from an injury. He's doing a very good job. He'll be out. You'll see him at walkthroughs and he's continuing to be able to do more and more. Uh obviously, you know, Storm's a person that I have a ton of respect for and and obviously you hate to see losing any guy due due to injuries, but uh we'll continue to to explore all sorts of options there and push our guys, but uh really uh Jawan's a pro, very intelligent. Um so he he's picking everything up, just not ready yet to do too much. Have >> you seen Morris kind of bring? >> Yeah, similar uh you know, local kid. excited to get our hands on him, get to work. Um, wired the right way. So, we'll get him with coach Callahan and just get to work. >> Is he here? >> Anything else? >> Uh, you going to be practicing outside today in the rain? >> Is it raining? >> Well, yeah, it was earlier, but the reason I as I mean, it was post on social media a couple weeks ago. I think you guys were out there practicing in the rain. I was just kind of curious if that's a philosophy [laughter] that or if that was just a shower popped up. >> Yeah. you know, you play in the elements in in this game and uh you know, I know we have some games that are indoors and those type of things, but if you can safely practice in the elements, I think it's good for you. I think it's good for quarterbacks to throw in the elements, wide receivers to catch in the elements, people to get their footing. So, as long as it's safe, uh we we'll certainly do that. Another quick story for you guys. So, when I was at the Vikings early in my career, I was I was the weather coach for Brad Childress. So, what a thankless job that is. Uh, so in the morning, and this especially in OTAAS in the spring, I would call the local meteorologists there in Minneapolis. I had three of them on speed dial and I'd ask them, this is before, you know, all these apps and everything, and I'd ask them, "Hey, we have practice at 11:30 a.m. What are you thinking?" So, we'd take in all this information, and then it was basically my call to say whether we're going to go inside or stay outside. So, there was one day the the meteorologists are just, uh, it's going to rain, it's going to pour, lightning, etc. So I tell Brett, Coach Childress, hey, we got to we're going to go inside and if you're okay with that, he said, "Sure." So the second we decide to go inside, I'm now doing a rain dance, praying that these heavens open up and it starts pouring. So here we are. We're in the indoor. This is Eden Prairie, the old uh Winter Park location. We're starting practice and it is so sunny outside. It is like gorgeous outside and we're practicing and I can still see Steve Hutchinson staring at me being like, "This was your call to come in here. This was you." So, I have PTSD when it comes to uh those type of decisions. Uh so, luckily I have we have better apps nowadays. Um but we'll always if we can safely practice outside, we'll go outside. More information than you guys care to hear. >> No, actually we're in the >> You're into more information. >> All right. Appreciate you guys. Thanks. Hey, [music]

title: Thad Brown: Bills Training Camp Returns To St. John Fisher University | One Bills Live
text: sports director from WOCC TV in Rochester when Thad Brown going to join us here on the line and uh Thad, we wanted to get you on obviously with the release of the training camp schedule for St. John Fischer University. Uh at first blush, what are your initial thoughts? I think we knew there were going to be some changes with Joe Brady taking over. How about that early casting call 8:30? Hello. >> Yeah, not a huge fan of that. you know, as someone who generally works a night job, uh, getting [laughter] up at 7 in the morning. If if there's not a tea time involved, then before 8:30 is generally not my thing at all. But look, like like you said, the first reaction to me was a reminder that when there's a new head coach, there's new rules. And this is how it works everywhere around the league. There's going to be new processes, new routines. I mean, when we get to the season, what Wednesday and Thursday and Friday is going to look like from a media point of view is going to be different. This is just how it goes. And I know, look, people in Rochester are not going to be excited about this at all. I mean, they we love hosting camp. We love that the Bills come to our town and and make Rochester their home base for what was three weeks in the past, now it's going to be two. So, anything that's reduced is going to be something that is not going to be uh met with excitement around here. But, look, it's still camp. Um, it's still seven practices and and for everybody who's an early riser, I think they will still have the same good time they've had the previous, you know, six or seven years under Shawn McDerm. >> I know that you've, you know, mentioned what the fans and what the city of Rochester will think. You know, certainly they would love a long camp and all that. What do you think it means, if anything, for the franchise, for the Bills. Why is camp short? Why does Joe Brady only go over there for eight or nine or seven or eight, nine practices? U, why do you think they're shortening it? And what benefit do you get out of I have my own theories I've shared with Brownie but what are your thoughts? >> I think initially this is the trend that the NFL has been moving towards the last 1015 years. I think when camp was in its heyday you know back in 2007 in terms of going away to camp around the league. There were I think 15 18 20 teams who did it. Now we're down to six or seven. It's been that way for a few years. So, I think what we're seeing again is when you go to a different coach, the likelihood is going to be that that coach will not want to go away to camp as much as Shawn McDermott did. Shawn McDermott was unique in his desire to go away. And I think the signal we're getting from Joe Brady is that this is not something that he prefers or wants to do. And remember, the Bill signed a three-year contract with Fiser last year. And when you think about the idea that that contract now was signed in what turned out to be the last year of Shawn McDermott for us in Rochester, that might be a bit for fortune uh fortunate because it's it's possible that maybe Joe Brady would not have wanted to come to roster at all. I don't know. I'm speculating. We're going to get answers from Joe Brady, I'm sure, when we get to camp in July. But I think the only way you read this is that the new coach is a lot like most coaches in the NFL where they don't prefer to be uh outside their home facility in camp. And I think the primary reason is not a comment on Rochester or St. John Fischer. The primary reason is that what teams have done to augment their home facilities is so good that spending time away from there is not the best way to keep your players healthy, the best way to get ready for the season. Again, it's not a comment on what they think of Roster St. John Fischer. It's just that the facility they poured all that money into at one bill's drive in Orchard Park is just a better place to be. And that's where most teams, most coaches want to spend their training camp time. >> I would say the other thing that's probably at least a contributing factor in how training camp is run is the increase in popularity with these joint practices. I think coaches feel like they've got more control over the tempo and pace of play in those settings where the head coaches quite literally have whistles at times. And the Bills are going to do that again this summer with the Cleveland Browns, uh, which was, you know, confirmed by Joe Brady and Brandon Bean. Um, there's some teams that that are doing two sets of joint practices. I know the Bears are doing that with the Bengals and the Titans in one preseason uh, alone. So, I I think this is only going to increase in popularity where every team in the league is going to be doing at least one set of these, if not two. I don't think we're uh as off the table to say that sometime long down the road that you can see the idea of these joint practices totally replacing preseason games as the way teams get ready for their season. that to your point, not putting a quarterback on the field to ever risk being tackled or your star running back or your best pass rusher when you can do that in a much more controlled environment of the joint practices then yeah I think certainly for the short term it's the better way I think for teams the better way teams believe to get ready for a season and going back to maybe not necessarily this year but in terms of the general opinion of what the Bills do with St. John Fischer. Fiser really is not set up to host a joint practice in the way many of these other facilities are. There was uh one with the Browns about 10, 11, 12 years back. If you really wanted to do it, you could. But when the way Fisher set up where you don't have two adjoining fields to have one giant space, which is generally how these practices are run, you have the offense on one and the defense on the other. It makes it more difficult and more congested to do what you want to host all the fans. So assuming the Bills want to go that route, you're right, most teams do. I do think that moving away from Fiser, there might be some connective tissue there. >> One of the things I had mentioned as well, if you want to give them the benefit of the doubt and say this is a one-off or maybe it's not the beginning of the end of the St. Sean Fischer trips over for training camp is that I think they will benefit this year in spending a lot more time in the new stadium in the preseason. Spend going over practicing in doing walkthroughs in it, getting used to the locker room, getting used to the ingress and egress, getting the players comfortable in that space so that when it they play a home game, it feels like a home game. Right now, it's an away game. I know what you're saying and you'd be the perfect person to answer this. I don't know how many more you need than the three weeks they would have if they had stayed at Fiser for another week because you would still have preseason week number two, preseason week number three, the off week before you even get into a game week. But you're right. I mean, this is everything is going to be brand new for the Bills going into this season. They don't know all the nooks and crannies. They don't have a comfortability like they've had with Highark Stadium. And I think for sure the more time you spend in that building, the better off you're going to be. I don't know how many regular camp practices they're going to hold over at the new stadium and that would be I think a good question for all of us to ask when we get to St. John Fischer in the end of July. Um even you know separate of just having the extra week that week that would normally be at Fiser will that be in the new stadium. How many other practices are you going to have during the year? To your point, Steve, it might make sense to have every Thursday practice in that stadium just to continue to get used to and get familiar with it even as the the seasons change throughout the fall. >> Last one I've got for you, Thad. Um, when training camp does open July 29th at St. John Fischer, what's like the one or top two things that you're looking to get answered that you know you're you're questioning and wondering about right now with respect to this team and their preparations for 2026? I think that the two position battles I'm looking at are are corner number two because everything I hear this team and especially the the defensive staff say about Davis and Igbonosin is how much they like what he does, what he brings. I think certainly he's got the the athletic ability and the makeup to be a perfect fit for this Jim Leonard defense. And then linebacker is the other one. You know, Dorian Williams is a guy who's been here for a while. He's had some chances. Hasn't really, I think, cemented himself as a guy you would believe in as a dependable every week starter. And again, in some of the same ways as Igbonosan seems to be impressive to this new staff. I think there's a lot of love for Caleb Alarms or and I share it. I'm excited to see what the the Bills uh rookie linebacker can bring. I think he's another guy that might fit this defense a little better. I like what he can bring off the edge in terms of another pass rushing option. So, those two position battles and I think to get a gauge on how much these two newer players, two guys that were brought in by the new defensive regime might really have a chance to be instant contributors. Both guys have, you know, their their uh reasons to believe in them in terms of just how good a player they were in college. They both have, especially Ignosen, you know, players that are holdovers that are um talented in their own right. I mean, Max Harrison, as long as you run a 4-2, NFL teams are going to find a way to use you. So, he still, I think, is the the favorite to be cornered to, but Ian, I think, has a real shot, and Alarm Zor is going to be a whole lot of fun to watch in camp. >> Uh, two-part question. It's my last one. Um, one, uh, they've got eight inside linebackers in camp, and we've thought that maybe, and maybe this is just something that Shawn McDermott liked, to bring in a Shaq Thompson or bring back a Matt Milano and all out the AJ Klene uh, stretch that was early in Mcderm's career here. Uh, they always had this veteran linebacker they would bring in, and they ended up playing and playing quite a bit. If they don't sign a guy like that, is it a signal that this coaching staff under Joe Brady is going to play young guys and they're not going to be afraid to do it the way some accused uh McDermott and his coaching staff of maybe making the young guys get on the field a different way? What do you think about signing a veteran guy here late in free agency right before training camp? And does it signal or are they going to be just forced to play a lot of younger guys that they've never been willing to do in the past? >> I think there's definitely a possibility they bring someone in. A linebacker would probably be my number one choice for if the Bills are going to add a veteran sometime late and it may be during camp. To be honest, I think they go to camp with the group they have right now. I think they're pretty satisfied with even what they have at linebacker and corner. Even though I think at corner when you get past Benford and the two younger guys, I think there there are a lot of questions. I think to your second question about whether or not it signals they were more willing to play younger guys. I don't know if I want to make a larger 30,000 foot view conclusion on what happens in this camp. I think this camp will be based more about how fast is alarms or develop into a guy you can believe in as a starter. How quickly is Igbonosen or even Haristston a guy that you think that you can put on the field every down and be okay with? I think trying to glean from that what this staff believes in in younger players versus older players in general probably is too early for us to to make that conclusion. I think it's going to be based on does the group we have look like a group we can go with or do we need help? And Brandon Bean has been very successful about finding guys late in what would generally be the offseason pro process whether it be July, August, even Brandon Cooks last year in November. So I think there's absolutely a willingness to bring somebody else in and for that player to be a significant contributor if they need that and I think they will determine that when we get maybe three or four weeks into camp. >> All right, Thad, thanks for the time. enjoy your uh five and a half, six weeks here because we're going to blink and we'll all be at training camp. We'll see you out there in late July. >> Sounds good, guys. Thanks for having me on. I got about 18 golf rounds to get in between now and then. We're gonna make some work on that right now. >> Yeah, best of luck in making that happen. I don't I know I'm not getting 18. And that's sports director Thad Brown from Wro TV in Rochester.

Brian Todd with ESPN. Um, what were your conversations with him?
