And when you guys get to Oxnard, um obviously that you got a little bit of a break after mini camp. >> Is that something that he'll he'll have to be worked in maybe a little differently than some of the other guys because he's not been the offseason program? >> No. Uh I mean this is you know he and I did talk about that a little bit. I mean he's going to be ready to go. Um you know he understands what's coming and um you know again if if we needed him to practice today he could. Um he's going to do some things. Uh but just uh as we close out the mini camp, you know, in the offseason program, there's no need for him to have to do the team stuff. He's going to get plenty of stuff with individual and and the mock stuff. >> And then one more. Uh Marshon Nean's girlfriend had a their baby. Uh I was wondering how do you keep in touch with the with the family and what they're doing and how do you keep Marshon's memory alive with >> Yeah, I appreciate you asking. We actually showed a picture of Mai today. So congrats to Catalina. I actually saw her a couple weeks ago at Demo's wedding. he was there. Um, and everybody's doing great. So, uh, the guys were fired up and excited and, um, you know, again, we've got, you know, different things. We've got, you know, a marker down in the players lounge supporting and and, uh, it says one love, big, you know, bright star because that was one of Maran's sayings. And, um, when you're part of our family, you're family for life. And so, uh, we want to make sure we do a great job of looking out for her and and baby Mai. Uh John Michelle with the athletic. What would you say is the biggest thing you're trying to get accomplished this week? >> Uh finish the installs. You know, doing the 8week, you know, offseason program where you normally you do nine installs and you get a couple review days. Uh I gave up those uh review days because I wanted I thought it was more important uh John to get the the rookies on the field at the same time for phase two with the vets. Uh so get all the installations uh through is one. Uh two is, you know, this will be the last chance for the connection piece and the brotherhood piece that we're working on. Um there'll be officials uh here for the next couple days. Uh Ron to Tolbert's crew is here. And then uh we're actually knocking out some league mandated um uh media uh meetings that we have to do um to lessen the blow when we get out to training camp just because those first couple days, the first day specifically of meetings is uh really long. And uh so we're going to knock out a few of those uh mandatory meetings. uh that we have to have. >> Is that the stuff with the officials or >> No, different things. Uh gambling, things like that, you know, different things that that go into to play and um so, you know, domestic violence, gambling, things like that. And so, um uh I just use it to try to get ahead of it and check a couple of those things off so when we get out to training camp, it's you still have a handful of things to do, but move more into football. uh one of the biggest stories in sports right now, Brandon Sorsby, um entering the supplemental draft or at least expected to. Would you guys have any any interest in him? >> Yeah, honestly, I know it's a big story line. I haven't followed it much. I'm aware uh just enough to be dangerous. So, I really don't have any honest opinions. Uh if we get to the point where we're interested, then certainly I'll have an opinion, but as of now, it doesn't affect my life and I'm focused on the 90 guys we got here. >> Nick Harris for Star Telegram. Kind of a follow-up to that. What does the scouting process look like for a supplemental draft guy? Did wherever you were in 19 Jaylen Thompson, how did that work for him? Is it something you refer back to in free agency for Jaylen Thompson? Like how does it >> Well, I can go way back, Nick, if you want to. I mean, I'm going back to Bernie Kar 1984. I think I was in like uh eighth grade, seventh grade, man. Uh it's just unique. It's different. I honestly don't even know exactly how it it plays out to be quite uh uh blunt with you. Um but uh again at you know at some point we'll get more involved in when that is and how it goes and um you know but uh at the end of the day um you know my focus right now is having three really good days of mini camp and uh and finishing off what I think's been an awesome awesome off season. >> A big topic with the players right now is the grass being used at all these World Cup venues. What's kind of your take on the situation and do you just kind of leave that to whatever happens? >> Yeah, no I mean I'm you know I get it. I'm a big uh actually World Cup guy. Uh I watch a lot of the games. It's been cool for me. I've been out by the uh the star watching the the watch parties and stuff that people have had and uh I think it's really cool. I'm going to the game next Monday. And so, um, you know, again, I think that at the end of the day, FIFA has their rules and the soccer players have their rules and our rules are, uh, a little bit different. And, uh, we feel like, you know, AT&T gives us a great home field advantage. And, uh, the turf is what it is. And we feel like it's one of the best turf surfaces in in the league. And so, um, but I am looking forward to going. I hope Messi plays. Uh, it'd be cool to see, uh, him, uh, Argentina. But, uh, yeah, that's kind of my thoughts. And then, uh, you know, sounds like they had the the blinders up, you know, the shades. So, it's not as majestic majestic as it is, uh, when we're playing our games, you know. So, the grass and the shade, I mean, it's just it's not as majestic. They just they're going to miss the experience. [snorts] [laughter] >> They're going to miss the sun, huh? They're going to miss the experience. >> I guess a quick one on Ryan Fenoy, just his development going into what he had last year going into this year. Um, what I would say, uh, just doing incredible, you guys saw it last year, I think 200 yard games. Um, you saw him really, you know, just do it on a consistent basis. It's not surprising. He'll be the first one on the practice field, he'll be the last one to leave. Anytime Dak wants to throw, he'll be out there. Um, you know, making himself available. I think that's huge. I think that's part of that meu factor that's so important when you're talking about uh quarterback uh receiver timing and and discipline and things like that. Um but uh just you know he earned it the right way. Earned it through special teams. Earned it by doing the run blocking, doing the things in the run game, the dirty work if you will. And now he's one of those guys that just, you know, because he does everything right. You know, Dak doesn't hesitate when he looks looks at him. He just turns it loose, throws it to a spot, and he's rewarded us with very very um big- time performances. >> Tommy Ar Dallas Cowboys.com. In this next month or so until you go to training camp, how do you and your staff make sure that your players keep on the playbook and the install so that when you get to Oxnard, you don't have to retach some things that you've been through this week or the last couple weeks? >> Yeah, I mean, it's part of the deal. Number one, we want these guys to get away a little bit. We think that's important. You got to recharge. It's a long season. I think that's good for all of us. Um, you know, the iPads that they have have all that information on it. You know, these guys have a really good plan. They understand, Tommy, that they're going to hear the same install, you know, of training camp day one of OTAA day one, and so on and so on. I think that's important, you know, but more more than anything, it's the coaches just checking in on these guys throughout the the deal. Why? Because we're not checking in on them. We care about them. We love them. We want to see, you know, where they are. Are they having fun? What are they doing? How's their family? How their wives, girlfriends, kids? Um, but they're pros and uh they know the importance of the uh FIB or you know football intelligence and um you know I think that uh these guys are pros and they're not going to need a lot of reminding. They know how important it is to get ready for training camp both physically but also mentally as well. >> And with the defensive personnel turnover you've had over the years or this year specifically as you've gotten to see these guys the last couple weeks. Who stood out to you in in a leadership role on defense? There's a lot of them. Um, you know, if I started up front, you know, Kenny Clark and Quinn, obviously Rashawn Garry, um, Donovan Rock who's got natural leadership ability from the linebackers. Um, you know, Demo certainly, uh, Dwinners has has leadership ability. Uh, Shamar's got great control of what we're doing in the secondary. U, Jaylen Thompson, PJ Lock, Malik Hooker's done a great job from a communication standpoint. Caleb DS has natural leadership ability. Uh you don't hear the corners quite as much, you know, on the outside, but a guy like Kobe Durant, you know, he's got natural alpha, you know, leadership to him. And uh uh I know I ripped off half the roster, but I think that's a good thing. >> Joe, uh Joe White, Dallas News. Brian, you kind of talked about the communication aspect there. Christian Barker was miked up and was kind of emphasizing the overcommunication aspect of things. With that being such an issue last season, how have you just kind of seen that transpired under Christian Barker just even in this early part of practice? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, day one, I mean, it really it started day one and I think you see it. It's verbal, it's non-verbal, but the emphasis when you sit in the meetings, it's like last year I felt like we didn't do a great job in meetings even talking. I know I talked about that, but it wasn't to the standard that I think it it should be or that it is now. um you walk into a meeting and you you probably need ear muffs because I mean literally these guys are hollering calls, close calls, riplets, whatever the calls are. And um when there's motions and change of strength, it flips a lot of things and you hear them all talking and really at all three levels. I think the other thing I'll say is that our defensive line is communicating differently than most defenses I've been around with their anticipation of what runs are coming, protection are coming based on formation sets and things like that. And I think that's got to do with number one how it's emphasized in every room, not just with the linebackers or safeties, um, but also the experience that we have uh, with our defensive line. >> This past season there was 22 tight ends drafted the most in over 20 years. Seems like the league really wants to go to 13 personnel. Meanwhile, you guys thrived in 11 personnel last year. Why do you think the league is kind of going into that? And I guess with you guys specifically and the receivers you have, is that something you want to get more into or is it just, hey, we got to play our cards? No, I mean, I think we're always going to try to play our best players, we I love our tight end room. Um, I think the reason teams are doing is it tries to simplify. If you talk to most defensive coaches, they don't have more than two or three calls that they probably use in 13 or 22 personnel. Uh, so it does simplify their hand more than maybe 12 and 11 and things like that. Um, but it's also you can do so many things out of it because you can spread them out in 13 against base defense and maybe find a matchup with a pass receiving tight end or a back or someone that can expose a matchup. Uh, but you also can get in close quarters and and pound the football. And so, um, we, you know, we did a lot of that in the red zone last year. Uh, maybe not as much out in the field, but uh, we also think that there's, you know, still a lot to getting our weapons and our speed on the field. And uh but the more that Scoon and Brev and Jake and um these guys, you know, continue to to grow, um it's and Hunter Leky, I'd be remiss if I didn't say Hunter. I mean, uh we we have those, but uh you have to decide, you know, who you want to put on the bench. >> Skyler Skyler Dixon with the AC running back position. I don't know if would you agree that it's kind of tilted sort of leaguewide from running back by committee days maybe a little bit back toward kind of a bellcow back and and how does the pass catching component of a bell cow back how big is that maybe compared to how we all sort of think of bellcow from the old days? >> Yeah, you know I I think honestly as I look around the league I think it's different in different places. I think there's different philosophies for different coaches and different teams based on roster makeup. You know, there's nothing that would make me and the offensive staff more uh ecstatic than for Jaden to take the step that we hope he takes uh because of the one-two punch that he and Javvante could potentially have and Jaden's ability to hurt you catching the football out of the back field. I mean, that's a dimension that we not didn't have, but that we didn't use as much because we chose to throw the ball to Cidi and George and Fergie and guys like that. But, um, I do think that it's different. Um, when we were in, you know, Los Angeles or San Diego, now Los Angeles, you know, we had a pretty good running back by the name of Leenian Tomlinson who was the bell cow and could score catching, throwing, uh, some throw touchdowns, uh, running. Uh, but we also love Darren Sprouls. And so it's like again if you have that guy that can do it all, but I do think that there's merit in having multiple people that can do different things because of the punishment that that position uh you know takes on. And so I think that that's where um you know you're going to have to play a second and third running back throughout the course of the season. So it's nice to have some depth and that's what we're trying to develop with Jaden and Phil and Malik Davis and um and guys like that. real quick, just since uh Clarence didn't ask, I'll hit the injuries. Um I can't believe he didn't ask. He was caught up on GP. Uh but uh so Malik Hooker is going to be limited today. He's got a tight back. Don Bland's doing great. Jaylen Thompson uh limited today, a little bit more individual with the pec. Azaraku is doing great. James Houston's got a back. And then Dak's going to be limited in uh uh team and just practice. He's uh got a sore knee. Nothing we're concerned about, but we're just going to be smart head knee last couple days. So, um, really healthy as of now. >> Babe, >> babe, 1053 Cowboys radio network. So, Brian, last week you, uh, talked about how you were going to be more involved in the defensive meetings and special teams meetings. Coach Landry, you know, famously handled all three, but it's a different time. >> Sure. >> Uh, have you thought about your, and obviously you're going to be the play caller. Have you thought about your allocation of time? There's still only 24 hours in the day. >> Sure. Yeah. Um it's different, you know, like right now I'm spending um I would say uh pretty balanced, babe, in terms of how much time with the offense, with the defense, uh with special teams. Um it's going to be different in training camp. You know, uh I might not be in all the meetings. I might be in the quarterback meetings more than I'm in the defensive meeting, but I'll probably go offset that by watching film with the defensive staff. So, now that we're getting into training camp, a little bit more longer days, more time, there's meetings, there's practice, there's walkthrough, there's practice, film review. Um, there's plenty of time to get it done. But, um, at the end of the day, um, you know, the job of a head coach, uh, is to oversee everything and make decisions that help you win a championship. And, um, kudos to all those guys that that did that. I'm not sure how many guys still do that today. Um, but uh uh my dad tried to do it and uh I think he did it pretty well. Uh but uh yeah uh I still get there's a picture right outside my office of Tom Landry and Roger Stalach on a chalkboard which again takes you back to now everything's technologically iPads and this and that powerpoints and so um you still can get a great product by doing things different way but you have to adapt with the the times. Sais with the athletic. Um, Brian, going back to like the 13 personnel question, even the running back, the league always has different trends that come in and out. How much do you try to get ahead of the trend sometimes and not just fall in line with what the league might be doing scheme-wise, but trying to see if you can develop something that could become the trend that, you know, other teams are kind of looking at? >> Yeah, I think, you know, you want to be curious. you know, you want to see what other teams are doing because there's a lot of really smart coaches and great players in the league that you should be studying and looking at. Um, I think we're we're a little bit different though is we don't just take someone's play or a concept or a coverage that someone ran and say, "Okay, we're just going to do it exactly that way. We're going to do it with what fits us." And um you know I think you know at the end of the day you know there's always a cyclical thing about the scheme in the National Football League. I think a lot of the trends odd come from college. You know you see them from high school to college. You know we all sit around Saturday afternoons watch college game and there's more space and things like that. But you know that's kind of a predictor of of where some things are going to come from. But uh believe believe me, when we're watching film of other people, uh we're looking not just for trends, but for okay, these are the schemes that we like that fit us. Because if you try to go steal something that doesn't fit you, like more than likely it's not going to work, you know, and again, we're not going to be a 50% 13 personnel team because we've got, you know, some receivers that if they're on the bench, they're going to be, you know, yelling at me and in my ear. And uh uh I think that uh we can still have the things that we need to keep the defense off balance, but at the end of the day, you have to have an identity. And I think that that's you know what we're curious what our identity is going to be exactly heading into this season >> and last uh last few years you've gone through the contract situation, which players just here. Um what have you learned about going through that with Micah, CD, Dak, and you know what delicate conversations are and not? Uh how how do you plan to approach that with George? Yeah, I just I'm authentic. I'm who I am. You know, I'm not the one negotiating contracts with these guys, whether it's Dak, whatever. If they come to me and ask my opinions, I'll give them my opinion. But at the end of the day, I'm not going to ask them about my contract or how much I pay for a house or this or that. Like, I mean, those are um personal decisions, but at the end of the day, I'm going to always support those guys. I'm going to be authentic. I'm gonna be real. Um you know, they know I'm there for them if they want to have those conversations, but you know, at the same time, I've got a job to do. And um [snorts] you know, I think that's the it's an easy answer, but it's it's the truth. You know, I'm you know, if if George wasn't here, you know, I don't care any less for George. I still love George. You know, I'm glad he's here, but like at the end of the day, the business is the business. And um you know, I have a relationship with these guys first and foremost. >> Patrick. >> Hey, coach. Patrick Walcows.com. Circling back to Jaden for a moment, he's saying things nowadays like he's more mature. He's quote, "I'm a different person than I was this time last year." He's leaning on the vets. Um, looking to practice and play to the standard. From a coaching standpoint, what does that do for you to see his development in such a short period of time? And what do you feel like he can be in year two? >> Um, well, one, I agree with with what he's saying. Um, I think he's come back with a different um, look on his face. I think he's practicing better. Uh, I do think that, you know, as he continues to grow, he's got to understand and realize that until he's the bell cow, you know, that there's going to be other roles he's going to have to fill, whether it's coming out of the backfield, catch the football, special teams. Um, but I I love the idea of a change of pace back to go with Javvante who is um just an absolute pounder, bruiser, you know, a guy that's going to, you know, score 12, 13 touchdowns every year for us. But, uh, Jaden's a huge part of what we're trying to do and he's got to do his part and I think he is doing his part. But, um, that's got to continue. Um, and this is not a knock at Jaden, you know, but like right now we're not playing real football. you know, we're not, you know, real football is when you got to pick up Demo coming off the edge in a blitz or you got to, you know, you got to run the ball in there and Quinn Williams standing in the hole or whatever. I mean, that that's real football. And so, um, I've seen a lot of great players that are awesome in shorts and then when you put the pads on, you're like, man, what happened? And, uh, I don't predict that for Jaden. U, but my point is I'm not going to get too high or too low on anybody. Um, right now, I'm just excited about the fact that he has matured. and keep into that position. You mentioned rightfully so, Javvante is a bruiser. Um, so is Phil Maf in his days at Clemson. He essentially had a red shirt year last year with the exception of the finale. What are you seeing from him and what kind of push can he make to get those reps at RB2 knowing that there's a little bit of redundancy with him being a Bruiser and Javvante? >> Yeah. Again, I mean, there's certain roles that, you know, he might fit better than Jaden, and there's certain roles that Jaden might fit better than than Phil, but at the end of the day, you know, I try not to have to call plays based on which backs in the game. You like the flow of the game to come to you as a play caller. So, really, it's the guy that does the most things the best, you know, and that's what you're thinking. But special teams is a huge part of it, you know, and so, uh, when Phil came back late last year, there was things we saw from Phil. His his his run instincts are are unique. Uh, they're they're they're elite. They really are. And, [snorts] you know, to evaluate him on last year alone is hard because of the shoulders and what he was dealing with and he really wasn't, you know, 100%. But again, another guy that I I think when the pads come on, you're going to get a great sense of of where Phil Mafa is. Garrett Podell, CBS Sports. Hey, Brian. Going back to defensive communication, how big of a difference is it length of play call defensively, whether it's like a couple phrases or a couple sentences? And um have you noticed a difference between this year and last year in that? >> Yeah, you know how CP um he's very convicted and short when he speaks, very direct. The play calls, I would say, are that way as well. Um, so, uh, you know, not that it's easier to call, but, uh, it's and I am the all-time guy and verbiage guy as an offensive guy, but it's it's cool to see, uh, these green dots kind of rattled those two or three words out of their mouths, uh, which is a little different than what we did last year. >> You had something else, >> uh, real quickly on on Jaden, is he limited or do you have a vision for him special team wise? You know, you usually a guy like that would be a returner. Well, he's not a returner. And so to get him on game day, what can he do special team wise? >> Yeah, it's a great point. Again, you know, whether we end up using one return or two returners, that's always something in play. Turp's obviously elite. Uh Jaden obviously would be an elite returner. He's also got gunner ability because he's fast. Um but there's certain restrictions that he has in other areas. Um but there's things he can do from a PP standpoint and stuff like that. He's certainly athletic enough, but the first two things would be gunner and returner. >> Yeah. Got to go. >> Good. Thanks, guys.

title: Dylan Fairchild's Offensive Line Impact for 2026 | Episode 268 Bengals On The Brain
text: [music] >> Welcome back, Mr. Goodberry. The First Star Logistics studio is fully equipped and ready to record. >> Welcome back to Bengals on the Brain, presented by First Star Logistics. I'm your host, Joe Goodberry. Continuing this little mini series we have in the off-season as we get ready for camp and all that to open up. We still got another month. Uh is a look back at some of these young prospects that the Bengals have that number one, we could use a jump in play, or I think we could expect one, or this guy's on the verge of being pretty good. And one of those is last year's best rookie, Dylan Fairchild, the third round pick out of Georgia that pretty much played every game at left guard. He missed a couple of D'Ante Smith and Quinton Spain to check in and play that spot, which was a fine. It's nice to have the veteran depth, but when Fairchild returned in the second half of the year, he was good. He went from okay, promising rookie, to he might be good, and he might be good right now. And his best game of the season, according to Pro Football Focus, he had about an 84 score in week 17 versus the Arizona Cardinals. Like, if that's who he ends up being, if that's his upside, he also had a great game, I think it was an 80 overall versus the Buffalo Bills a couple weeks before that. I was going to go with that one originally, but it was in the snow, and I thought you're not going to get a great evaluation of the defensive line in that game. So, let's go with the Cardinals. Less talent on that defensive line, but that's okay. We get uh probably a cleaner evaluation. We can't say, "Oh, it's just cuz the the snow." Because we've had that in Buffalo where Jackson Carman had a great game and it really didn't really mean much. But, the frequency of Dylan Fairchild's good game started happening more often in the second half of the year. Culminating in this game against Arizona Cardinals, which we didn't do a film review on uh in on Bengals on the Brain during the season because we just did a Dylan Fairchild review, I think, the week before that. So, that leaves us with Dylan Fairchild versus the Cardinals. Check out these reps. And this is what the upside looks like and what we're hoping to get in 2026. >> Number 63 is Dylan Fairchild at left guard there. And we've got about 70 plays cued up. The Bengals get out to a big lead and the backups come in eventually. But, until then we are only going to stop at the plays that make sense as our old pal, Akiem Davis-Gaither, knocks down the first pass of the game intended for Ja'Marr Chase. But, this is his highest-graded game of the year. He and Orlando Brown are going to double-team on a lot of plays here, as you'll see. Orlando Brown and giving a shove to Calais Campbell before Dylan Fairchild has to get him out of there and he really can't. Probably probably should get a better help from OBJ there at left tackle. But, after that, I think we're going to get about eight or so very nice blocks from Dylan Fairchild and maybe just two or three bad blocks, which is a great ratio. Cuz normally, it's like five and five. All right. He and Ted Karras getting the double-team there as the pass goes to Tanner Hudson. Nothing really to talk about there. I think uh Karras struggled in this game, if I remember. I want to say Marius Mims misses a couple of drives as Cody Ford comes in. Fairchild here. Good job getting in front of 94, but it's a boot that goes to Drew Sample. Had me cuz the Bengals don't do that too often. Although, if I remember correctly in this game, they do it a handful of times. Towards the end of the year, we started seeing more under center play action boot, naked boots, extra jumbo lineman, full back usage. Here we get Dylan Fairchild. Let's refocus our film review here. Against 55, he and Orlando Brown Jr. are going to get 55 out of there, man. Absolutely throwing him out of the club, and Chase Brown puts his head down with the kind of one cut up field for 3 yd. We're going to see some good Chase Brown runs in this game, as well. So, a good game for him to end the year. Well, you still have week 18, but they kind of acted like this was the end, the way they played. All right. 55's going to go with the power this time on Fairchild. He does a good job of re-anchoring. Look at him losing the initial battle here. Gets his hands out, brings them back in, latches inside right there, drops his butt, drops his weight, even though he's getting the legal hands to the face, keeping Joe Burrow clean for the deep shot that doesn't get completed. Looks like it bounced off Tee's hands, I think. I don't I don't think Burrow got his hand on it. I don't remember correctly, now. All right. Fairchild again here. Going against 95, he's diving inside. Do we got a stunt? Nope, just keep hammering him then as Burrow tries to run and get something. Kind of throws it away, throws it up to Yoshi. Third down. Okay. Fairchild here has got his eyes outside. Do we got a blitz potential coming? He and Calais Campbell doing a good job sticking with him. Here comes a nice open window throw for Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase. Well, Johnson tries to rip it out. Ja'Marr does a good job staying with it. Strong hands there. Do we ever find out what the rock, paper, scissors was? All right, Fairchild. Stunt, for sure. He could tell by the way 90 released like that, right? As soon as he goes out to the outside, he goes, "Okay, I know what that looks like. Let me work my way back in here." As that ball goes to Ja'Marr Chase for a gain of four. Ball comes out so quickly in this offense. That is a big advantage for a lot of guys. You know, they're the Bengals pass a lot, and it puts a lot of stress on the O-line. But, half the passes are so quick that it really doesn't matter cuz they can lose and still not give up a pressure. All right, Fairchild and Orlando Brown going to 90 here, and then Fairchild's going to have to release once he gets his hand off of him. You see his white glove get on the forearm. He's going to disengage and then go get Cody Simon. And Chase Brown's going to get uh 4 yd out of it. A lot of cutback running in this Bengals offense. The cutback guys have to do a a good job of getting the defenders out of there. We could probably get more explosive runs once the backside guys start getting their guys on the ground. I like this again for Fairchild. He's got to come all the way over to get 90. Even though Collier is going to punch him, he's going to get in position to stay in front. And uh Chase Brown does just enough to squeak and get 3 yd, so. Oh, that's P Ryan, I'm sorry. P Ryan puts his head down for 3 yd. And then we get a quick touchdown pass to Ja'Marr. I don't think we have anything for Fairchild here. Yep, ball's out very fast. Smoke route, spot route. This isn't a screen because nobody is screening the defenders, if that makes sense. If that's a question, I'd like to not do that this year at some point, not talk about what the difference in screens are, but if you if you want to know, we can spend time on it. Just being flexible, accountable and hungry. >> See you all season long. >> What are you trying to accomplish? >> To get fast, physical and continue to build off of this camp. Don't want to lose the the work we put in this whole month. Come back in shape, ready to roll. >> What coaches actually did you How do you work out with How do you work out some of some of those things or changes you >> Uh yeah, I mean a bunch of things. You got things you can do in the weight room. Uh and there's things you can do like jump rope, cone drills. Like there's You can do with field work. Are you asking like specifically or just in general? >> in general. >> Yeah, just in general those things. >> Where did you do some of that work this off season? >> Uh some of it I was back home on the west side and then I was down in Fort Myers at X3 training with Jordan Llewellyn for month and a half. >> Did you do that for the pre-draft this year? >> Correct. Yeah. Yeah, I really liked it there. >> What's the comfort level in year two? You know, you always talk to to guys going into year two, and they just seem calmer and more relaxed. Everything comes a little bit easier. Is that kind of what you're feeling right now? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I've told people like coming into your sophomore year, like compared to rookie, it's just so much more. I wouldn't say relaxing cuz you I don't think in football you can ever really relax. Like you got to have an edge about you, but just being so much more comfortable, uh not only like just being familiar with like the guys, and I'm not like trying to learn names and stuff, but also with the offense, we have a lot of translate from last year. Uh so, it's just a lot more comfortable, and I feel like I'm able to play a little bit faster, doing a lot less thinking this year. >> Scotty has kind of said that this team as a whole is spending more time on the field, more time getting discussed things just cuz you don't have to learn as much. Do you do you kind of feel that? Do you think this team is in a place where you can focus on more of those small things and not trying to learn everything all over? >> Oh, absolutely. And I I think that's the biggest thing from last year to this year is just like I wouldn't call it simple, but it's just like I feel like we're trying to nail the basics before we start adding on stuff. Uh I felt like there were times last year where we were just kind of like throwing a lot, and we had to kind of sift through it and figure it out. I feel like this year we've done a good job like mastering the basic things, uh especially during this OTA period where we can really, you harp down on those things, and then just building off those as we go throughout the weeks and then into training camp. >> Isaac, we saw your role expand last year once Dan took over. Play calling, more snaps per game, a few more targets per game. Did you feel that over the past nine over the last nine games? And like what kind of platform does that provide for you entering into year two? >> Yeah, uh I definitely felt a little bit of a shift. I don't know if it was play calling or is it just comfortability overall with um you know, being a new guy and just trying to uh learn my place on the offense, so I don't know exactly what the shift I like what caused the shift, but yeah, I definitely feel like uh as an offense, we got a lot of weapons, and I'm I'm excited to see how we utilize them in this next season. >> You're starting year two, but Dan said in his press conference earlier that you approach the game like a veteran. To hear that from your head coach heading into your second season, I mean, does that tell you you're doing things the right way? >> Yeah, absolutely. But I don't want to like hang my head on that and say, "Oh, I've done a good job, know, pat myself on the back and keep going, but I always want to have an edge about me and kind of have that mentality of being a rookie where it's like, you know, you got to do everything the right way in order for the coaches to even notice you and once they notice you, then you got to keep building on those things and making plays and then they'll be comfortable with you. So, just keep building on those things and just become more and more reliable on the field. >> You mentioned the skill guys. What's the excitement level of just playing in this offense in a bigger role, you know, and there's so many good football type guys that can catch the ball for everybody >> Exactly. >> and be some 101 situations there. How excited are you to potentially get a little bit more of that >> Yeah, I mean, it's exciting for me. It's exciting for the whole offense just cuz I mean, with the weapons that we have, I don't know how you're going to guard all of our skill positions. I feel like if you want to try to double a guy, then you're just leaving another extremely skilled person wide open. So, I think it's a great opportunity for the whole offense. They got to worry about a lot of guys and I'm we're excited to punish them on the field. >> Earlier I asked >> Go ahead. >> Earlier I asked Dan about the Knicks title run and seeing them in their drought, you know, the Lions fan and their drought and not being able to win a Super Bowl. You've been a being a Michigander, long time Lions fan. Did you take a moment watching them win the title like kind of sit back and like, what will it be like to win a title with the Lions? >> So, I'm going to be completely honest with you. I didn't watch a single game of the NBA Finals. [laughter] I just I could never get into it. I don't know why. I've just always been an NFL guy. Like I watched one NBA game this year and it was the one that I went to and it was actually the the Pistons beat the Knicks by like 40. So, when people are like, I don't even know who's in the finals. Like, who's in the finals? Like, oh, it's the Knicks. I was like, what? We killed the Knicks. Like, why are the Knicks in the finals? And then they won it, but if I had been watching, yeah, I mean, it's always surreal to see, you know, the champions and it would be nice and it's obviously our goal to be able to hoist that and have a parade down, what's the name of it? Woodward? Yeah. So, I think that's all our that's all our goal this year. >> I think more guys any goals personally as you see this year in training camp and do you care to share any of that with us? >> Uh, keep them personal, but yeah, I do have some goals for sure. >> Yeah. How I guess how much loftier are those goals than compared to say last >> Yeah, I mean last year I came in not really knowing what to expect. I don't know how much playing time I was going to get. I was really just working on earning my role. So, this year now that I feel like I've got a little more comfortable and yeah, I I have some pretty lofty goals for myself, I'd say. >> One more guys? >> How much different do you feel I guess now versus say at this point last year when you were coming in, you know, brand new to the you know, the NFL and the experience and and having made your own mark? >> Yeah, I think [snorts] like I kind of talked about earlier, it's just comfortability. Obviously, I don't have the game mastered by any means. I'm on year two. Like I'm still a year or two player. Still coming in, still have a lot of things to learn, but like you said, I do have a year under my belt, so I can, you know, learn from the things I did last year and build on the things that I did well and just continue to grow and grow with this offense. >> What are your first impressions of being out here with the guys and with everybody here and now? >> Mhm. Uh, it's been fun being out here. We playing football. I feel my element. I feel like it's all our element, you know, just being out here to be able to get on the grass and do what we do and compete. It's been fun. >> You're uh filling some important shoes while while they're sitting out. Do you feel any pressure on that coming in from the outside? >> Never been pressure. It's to me it's football, you know, um regardless of how it go, who's up, who's down, you just always got to be ready and I think for me, any player in this league, you know, that's what you train for, for the moments, for your opportunity to come. Whenever your opportunity comes, I'm I just look at how I got my my start in this league. You know, I wasn't a starter, but in a matter of a week, you know, I became a starter, green dot player, captain of the defense. So, it's like you got to be ready for whatever in this league. >> I noticed like between reps, you're talking a lot with the other guys. How's the communication flow going on for you guys? >> Yeah. It's been good. I think that's just how you learn how to be able to play and play fast. And uh it just comes with natural communication. Like off the field as well as on the field, you know, this past weekend we kind of got together watching film. And there's actually some things that happened today that just naturally came with our conversation over having having over the weekend. >> Sheldon, can you tell me what those conversations were like? >> Just talking about certain routes that we've seen and how another person see it, you know what I'm saying? And then it is actually good, you know, hearing another person's perspective and how he watches film as opposed to how you watch film and seeing it from a different person who like who plays a different position. So, there's certain routes and just talking about where we was going to jump or what not. >> Did you get one of the interceptions today? >> Uh no, it wasn't an interception, but it was actually a couple breakups, yep. >> You guys picked off a lot of passes, got your hands on a lot of passes today. That's definitely a point of emphasis. Is that something that you've been around like in the past or where else have you been? >> Definitely. You get the ball back to the offense so they can go put up points and we do it again. That's That's the name of the game. Defense go get the ball. >> And Shep talked about how how quickly you stepped up as a leader in front of the guys in this room with your experience. Just Is that something that you are mindful of stepping and trying to, you know, make sure that your voice is heard or is that just kind of a natural thing? >> I just think it's my personality. Uh being a safety on defense is similar to being a quarterback on offense, you know. You got to learn the whole defense. So, I think that was my main thing when I first got here early OTAs phase one just trying to learn everything, the plays, the calls, talking to myself in the room. So, then when I'm on the field and I'm saying it, it's just the same thing I that I did like when I was a rookie. Just getting comfortable saying the calls so when you out there in the field and you are talking and making your checks and what not, you just feel comfortable doing it and you don't uh am I saying the right thing or not. >> And Shep talked about how I guess mature like you are in your studies. Is that something you really been or have you grown into that naturally? >> Yeah, they used to joke with me uh like my first two, three years, you know, they would just say I had a older personality, older soul and I mean, it's cool with me, you know, I feel like it slowed the game down for me, you know. My first My first year definitely I'm, you know, like a a rookie out there, you know, just all over the place, but then you start slowing the game down once you start getting that experience and what not and it just naturally carry over. >> Did anyone ever tell you that like before football like as as a kid for you? >> Nah, nah, nah. Yeah, I never really heard that off like before football. >> We've heard a lot about your personality, but what about like your actual physical game do you think you're bringing to this defense? I mean, I like to be physical physical player, you know. I do whatever the team ask honestly. I mean, I'm going to give my everything. I'm sacrifice my body, lay my body on the line. I mean, I think that's any player in this league, but that's just how I feel going into any game. If it's truly something that's bothering me, I'm going to try to go play regardless. The only thing that I feel like I mean, you look at my career history like that kept me off the field was something I really couldn't play through, you know, but I'm going to sacrifice my body and lay it on the line. >> Well, I mean, given that you play with that physical style, how what's the key to having a long NFL career? Hey, what 80 games? That's That's kind of phenomenal given how physically you play. >> I mean, it's a little grace and favor, but I mean, you also got to do the work, take care of your body as well. I mean, the weight room is a big part of that, you know. I I firmly believe in that. Like you got to got to, but you also got to, you know, stay on top of the body work, recovery, stretching, everything. Just It's not one specific thing. It's just a accumulation of things, honestly. >> And with that meeting that the the DBs had, who who kind of got that together where was it? >> Mhm. Uh it was DJ. He just, you know, reached out to the group message. He was like, "Yo, I'm having film, little food at the house. Y'all come over." You know, and and I've I've seen that at different places I've been before and I I respected it, you know. Like yeah, let's go over here and let's watch some film. So, it was a good time.

title: Detroit Lions assistant coaches meet with the media | June 16, 2026
text: Yep. Another year, man. Just good to be back. Um, a lot of the same people in the building, a lot of new people in the building, but overall, it's just been a great all season. We've been able to, you know, we're a lot further along. We feel like we've been in a lot of years. Uh, just the transition uh on offense and then defensively having new people in. Um, bringing some guys with new roles. It's it's been a really really good offseason so far, though. Uh we we probably put in more work this off seasonason on the grass and in the class than than we've been had the ability to over the last few years, but this is this has just been a great great offseason so far. >> Why why is that? Why you been able to put in more work? Obviously no rookie mini camp this year. >> Yeah, I think two days instead of three. So where are you putting those? >> Yeah. So I I think when when you think about just the repetition of what we're doing like it was a lot less learning I think for our guys this year. So the process of learning can kind of slow down the process of reps. Uh the process of learning takes a lot more time in the building of doing this. Now we're actually talking through the details of how the rep should look versus what the rep should be. Uh I I think all around uh whether it's in our in our front was the skilled guys, receiver, quarterbacks. I just think us being on a page a little bit earlier than we've been even in the past few years has been really good. and JG and and you know and Saint and Paneet uh then Hutch a lot of those guys have just really they it's just been a huge drive for those guys that are up top and our leaders and the people behind them have done a great job following so a lot more detail in the reps that we're getting >> year by year we've continue to see Jameson's grow as a receiver what is your charge this offseason where do you see what is like the next level >> mentality um you know we've really worked as hard this offseason even just even on the phone talking about the detail that it takes to go from being good to truly elite uh in our game. Uh and then the things from a mentality standpoint of uh the way that we go about we working like not even just uh the start of a drill, but also just the finish of everything that we do, his detail, his eyes, uh his catch points, his checkpoints, uh everything that we're doing now or we did March, April, man, it showed up. We we're really excited about where he is right now. This is this has definitely by far been his best off season, his best, you know, chance to grow as a player since we've been here for uh a number of reasons, but he's done a good job. >> Same question with with Isaac. What was your sort of message to him heading into this year? >> Yeah, we we try to do a good job of coming out of the season talking about, you know, where we wanted to be. Short area quickness was something that we wanted to improve. Um, and that gives him the ability in those one-on-one situations to not just win with length, but to win with quickness and length. That gives, of course, JG just a even bigger window to throw the football. Uh, he's done a good job of going and getting, you know, the football since he's been here. And then now at the top of his breaks, they they're so much cleaner. He's so much stronger. Uh, last year, what I like to do is I like to watch uh where we were. Um, especially from an athleticism standpoint to where he is now. It's not even close. He had some knee uh soreness last year. Uh this year he came in was able to work on the things before and not after. So we look forward to him really really growing. >> Just knowing the player um in Jer Gibbs, what will allow him to have the success if he is truly used as a bell cow running back this year? >> Man, uh just you know opportunities. I I think everybody knows what this kid is and we got to keep him healthy. Uh we we got to do a good job on the perimeter of keeping him healthy. We got to do a good job on the interior of keeping him healthy and and just playing through the echo of the whistle. The biggest thing about Jir, he's not down. You know, you think he's going down, he's not down. He's going to come out of the back of there. At the same time, if you don't finish the play, you know, late hits on backs, different things on backs, it can slow him down. So, our biggest detail in our room and up front is just making sure that we protect his opportunities. Uh, because we know he'll do he'll do the rest with the football. >> The departure of Khif is more than production. It's obviously all the intangibles that he brings to your room. I'm just curious. You bring in a guy like Greg Dorch, young guy, hungry guy, kind of fills some similar roles in the scheme. What What have you liked about Greg and your early interactions with him in the classroom and on the field? >> Yeah, so fit first of all. Um, you know, he he can handle being a good player in the room with great players as well. Uh, I think that Saint does a great job of leading in the room. J Mo has really stepped into more of a leadership role uh rule ro role in the room and Dorch has taken that and so that's that's the first thing you know fit right after that we come to the grass he has unique short area quickness as well he can catch it in traffic and come through some of those uh we're looking forward to seeing what he can do more when the shoulder pads come on of course right now it's a little bit difficult but to see all of the things that he can do but what he's been able to do he's been able to grasp a couple of different positions at the receiver position so that flexibility also gives us something that that that Leaf at one time could give you without even thinking about it. So, he's done a lot of great things so far. Can't wait to see him in the, you know, in a real training camp with the pads on. Really excited about where he is right now. >> And in what ways has Jameson stuck with us in the locker room? >> Uh, I think more it's more so I I can't speak to the locker room. You know, coach is not, you know, I ain't going in there. Well, don't go in there. But in the classroom, the one thing that has really, you know, surprised a lot of us and made us feel better is uh his ability to be vocal and ask questions about the why, you know, why is his depth that, you know, the fifth time outside foot hit and this one is very similar. Well, it's the reason because the option route under has maybe been reduced a yard or two. Now that he understands all that is conceptual football and now that he gets the concept of it, he also understands how we go attack. So, if he's helping one of our young guys, uh, and we have a rap option, he understands now, listen, man, you can't get any higher than three yards on this, and this is why. So, that's what we're seeing in the room. Now, >> coach, I know Kendrick L had the unfortunate injury, but just just getting to know him so far. What What do you think he can bring in the team, >> man? Strong, fast, physical, uh, two position flexibility already, really came in with his head in the right place. Our guys, they they fell in love with him immediately because he does have the grit that it takes to play with us. um very disappointed and and frustrated for him uh because he physically was ready. His body was ready. He was his body, you know, coming from where he came from and and and from the SEC to to this was a is an easy transition physically for him. Really wanted to see how it worked out in training camp, but you know, I like where he is right now. He's working his butt off every day to make sure that when he comes back, uh we'll get a lot out of him. He's a good pick. Like him like him a lot. silver lining there is opportunity for somebody else maybe that's a silver lining with so some guys in that area the depth chart what do you like about that group Tom Kenny Don Mclo >> it's stacked it's a really stacked group uh and I think because of that that's going to let our you know our ones now even go to a higher level because now they are competing those guys that are competing for that second area when they get a chance to make a play if it's a big play the ones feel that so now the ones are going to go level. Uh TK, uh Dom Love it, Malik, uh newcomers, Sid, Abdorch, all these guys are in there now and it's just this huge competition to where the hardest part is I'm I'm trying to make sure that I'm getting everybody the same looks in different situations. So, the quality control behind their opportunities is probably what's most important. So, if I come out of uh this in training camp, I want to see a certain skill set of each one of these guys matched against each other, not necessarily just their best skill set versus someone else's uh skill set. >> You took stock of everything. Where did you feel like I mean you can improve? And how much you know is the vertical passing game kind of an area I guess that you guys would like to see a little bit more? >> Yeah, we Yeah, we definitely want to be able to marry what we do maybe just a little bit better. Uh you know, run game, pass game. You always want to do that when you come out of years. But where I felt like we could have got better is there's explosives out there in the run game. There's explosives in the pass game that either a lack of detail, uh, a not a connection that wasn't made throwing catchwise. Those are the things you you don't you don't get those fixed in the season, man. You got to have those things ready to go. And right now, I feel really good about where we are. >> How valuable was it to add Cedric Wilson to that room? >> Huge. It was huge for us. At the time, you know, we thought he was still a good player. We didn't realize how quickly he could pick up the the playbook. Uh he's three position functional. Uh he he has a large catch radius. He understands our route game. He has a certain level of smoothness to him that those outside guys have to have, you know. >> Thanks. >> I know you are involved as all the coaches are in the scouting process. When you were watching his tape, what did you see in his game that just screamed that guy can play for me? >> Uh contact balance with the ball in his hands. receivers, you know, especially young receivers, one of the easiest things it is to do for him is to get them on the ground. This was a guy, and there was a couple other guys in the draft that we really liked like that. He was a guy that could get his hands on the ball, make a play in space, but it wasn't all about making someone miss. We're going to need four to eight yards sometimes that we need to go through guys or get on edges of guys, and that's an elite skill because that's a chain mover. >> Absolutely. >> You guys have I think threw 60 fewer play action passes last year. And how much did that have an effect also like maybe on the vertical pass game because no doubt just the way that you know defenses are set up with the field. >> Yeah, the reduction of the run action pass game has a lot to do with how efficient you are on first down as well, right? If you get behind on first down now, the efficiency of faking the ball like you're going to run it in the second and 17, second and 18, you can't have those. So the TFL's are what's probably most important for us adding to our running action game. we get our TFL fixed, the way that we block things on the perimeter, then our run action pass game will create more explosives down the field. Yeah. >> Entering the season, did you see anything different in how he approached this year or just his mentality entering this year? How what have you seen out of him preparing for the road that he's ready to take this year? >> You know, that's that's been one of the biggest things of me and our conversation with Job once he finished the season last year was the fact that I wanted him to start faster at the beginning of the season. And so going into the off seasonason, how he prepared his body, uh doing some MMA training, training out there in Cali, uh with Saint doing some different things so he can come back so he's looked the best he's looked so far in his pro career pro career. And so for him, the biggest thing was to make sure that he understands his responsibility. Um, his responsibility from the head coach cuz when the head coach tell you, uh, he's giving you the keys and you have the responsibility for everybody in the organization, every kid, every fan that's a Detroit Lions fan. So my onus is to put that on him and he has to handle that. He has to handle it well. So for him to be in the best shape that he can be in, uh, praying for no injuries at all, but the fact that he's smarter, he understands the offense. So I'm I'm excited for him. He has a big role to play and I and I'm I'm really I'm really to see what level he plays at >> You mentioned the uh MMA training. Is there any aspect of training the mind within that as >> you know with training? Let me let let me say something. When you train in the offseason, you put your body through different things. So you can handle the rigor of the season like how hard the season really is. And so when you do MMA training, a lot of times most people don't understand boxing, when you punching is all about hand placement and hand eye coordination, balance, putting the weight on the balls of your feet, the same thing you do when you in pass protection, the same thing you do when you running and playing on the outside foot. Guys got to understand how those all sports all correlate to each other. That's why you should play all sports. And so when you do MMA training, your abs, your core, striking, power through the ground, all those things affect. So when he does that kicking, extending your legs, hamstring, your quads, all that stuff takes trainers. But the mental part of it is just the aspect of always having what I would say um putting yourself in a situation where you're training in April, but you see, you see January, you see February. That's the biggest thing. It's the mental aspect of it. You know what I mean? Making sure that you're training right now for a goal to get later on. And so that's why I try to tell the guys when they're training off season. >> I spoke to a check a couple weeks ago. was asking about the relationship you guys have right now. He said, "Oh, the coach I've been needing." You hear that and the relationship you guys form. What has it been like when you do that? >> You know, for me, man, like as a as a former player, you you you hate it when a coach told you a good job and you knew that wasn't the right thing to do. When you go back and look at the tape for me to Z, I I always and it's hard for me most of the time because when I see guys play, I see what they do wrong. I see all the things that I want to get better at. And for him, he's very coachable. And so when you have a coachable player who has the experience, played on two Super Bowl teams, was a starter, and played a lot of a lot of meaningful minutes, for me is to get him to be the best he can and be the most efficient I can get him. And so every little thing that he does, his alignment, his tracks, his landmarks, his eyes, I'm on him by every single thing. And when you when you coach and you want guys and you want to be great, you want coaches to get on. You want them to tell you there's always ways to get better. And so for me to him, I always want to make sure I coach the person, the player, but I love the person. So my biggest thing is to get to know who Zay is. I call him Zay. I get I want to know who he is, what the things he's been through. And then once I go through that part, then I can coach him. I can say whatever I need to to say to him on his grass because he know at the end of the day, Coach Choice rock with me. He love me. But second of all, he going to make sure I'm trying to be the best I can be cuz he going to have to play big for us this year. And so for him to understand that, I think he he respects that, man. I got man like it's a all players I coach man I want them to feel the same way so I respect that from them. I'm going keep going. >> I know in the pajama phase but how quickly has responded to it like in the moment when you're pointing out those >> uh quick and it's and it's day by day and that's the thing you want to see just each and every day somebody to continue to get better and that's one thing that I realized about Zay like I can coach him on something and you can see him come out on the field the next day and he's working at it and as a coach that's the biggest thing that you want especially in this this part of the year. So once we get to the fall, he has the confidence of everything in the offense cuz he's new to the system. And so having confidence in the offense so he can be ready to roll. >> Vaky is something we've seen a lot on special teams, but where is he at last year? A lot of stops and starts, but where's he at with his development at running back? >> Vaky Yaki. I love Vaky. And Vaky is one of the the he's probably the best kid you can possibly get. A salt of the earth type of person, but I'm probably the one that cuss Vaky out the most. I'm sorry to say it. Mama got to forgive me. But the biggest thing for me to Vaky is is when you have a player with the talent level, he's explosive, he's fast, he's smart, he's physical, and so he's putty still. You know, he had a lot of injuries last year. Had to have a chance to really be hands-on with him so much. And he's a one of our best guys in the league and special teams. And so for him this off seasonason, you can see the development. You can see the work ethic. I can get on Vaky all day. I'm going to probably get on him the most, but he never never complains, gets back on the field, does what he's supposed to do, and he works his tail off. And so when you got people like him that works hard, and then he wants to get better, that's the easy part for it's easy to be a coach when you have guys like that. So I got to continue to to to push his envelope. But for me, to him, man, it's just it's been remarkable to see him work through the injuries, get back this year, and really work at his craft. It's been good for him. >> Going back to PCO, obviously in Dallas, you you know, kind of had a similar role with Wayne behind Marco, >> what kind of mentality did you have to have to kind of, >> you know, play that role? And also like how many touches do you need to kind of be effective in your >> and you know, I guess >> that's that's that's that's huge what you asked. You know, as a when you when you preparing for NFL as a running back, you always got to prepare as a starter because you always know you want to play away. And so for me to for me to say was the simple fact like whenever you get your opportunities, you got to make the most of them. is very huge because it's plays in a it's plays in a game that are critical yards, critical pickups, critical catches that you have to make that we didn't make last year. So, um, coach has been coach Fitz has been a great mentor of mine for a long time. I've known him since I was like a sophomore in high school. So, um, going on the better part of almost 15, 20 years now. So, Coach Reed, I mean, Coach Coach Fitz, not Coach Reed, but Coach Fitz has been a great mentor of mine. Well, you have to problem solve different things every day. There's always things you have to work for, work towards, um, getting everyone on the same page, whether it's just simply like scheduling or, you know, um, you know, things from the football side of it. But then there's a personal element, too. You know, you're you're talking with kids and I've been in those shoes as a player before, but 19, 20, 21 year old kids who've got real world problems, whether they're dealing with family, whether they're dealing with um, things in their, you know, kind of arena. So, you know, you have to be able to make sure you reach and touch point a lot of different groups. Like, how much are you looking for that guy to to step into the six though? >> Well, selfishly now as a tight end coach, you want it to happen zero times because that means it takes one of your guys off the field. It's it's definitely great for you know all offensive knowledge of it and for you know being able to kind of have a have your hand in all the pieces of it. It's it's it's a great time for it and I I you know 13 personnel 12 personnel as a tight end coach you love it but also I mean look at all the weapons we have on the offense you know we're deadly in 112. What are you looking for growth for him in his his fourth year? Uh, I think it's just, you know, Sam being the best version of himself, you know, and, you know, getting where, you know, he's feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feel feels great in all three phases and just continue to hone down the little techniques, you know, little route running things here, a little, you know, footwork and hand placement in the run game, you know, protection wise. I think he's he's like you said, he's done a great job in all three and just continue to see him, you know, improve on those every single time he gets a chance to. impressive or unique is that mindset to come out franchise records as a rookie as a receiving option, but to to put the work into being a better locker that he has. text: So this is how this week will look when it comes to injuries. We're pretty clean for the most part. The only person that won't be out there today will be Kate. They've been focused. They've been detailed. We understand exactly how OTAs is as far as the physical part but the mental part and the movement skills is something I've been focused on and making sure that the execution of what we're trying to do offense defense and special teams is on point. So I think that's been pretty good for us. So other than that any questions? >> What did what did Tretton show you last year and you think that this time last year he was competing with Josh for the center spot and you just come in. What so what did you learn about him through the course of last year? >> Character first and foremost of a guy that was competing at the center spot and that's something that we've done with a number of guys is try to create competition and once we had the injury to AVT man he was more than willing to move over to the guard spot. And and then just take on that job and he didn't complain. He didn't say anything about it. Only thing he coach what do you need us to do? I mean we've just stabilized that part of it and the continuity more than anything is what's important when you especially have those five guys that can play together for a long time. So look forward to seeing those guys get to come together more with communication things like that. So I'm excited about that. >> When you talk about stabilizing how much of an emphasis was there with you and Darren to bring stability to the organization overall and maybe operate differently than previously? Yeah, I think that's one of the things that that you want to do as a coach and GM is is start to talk about how do we stabilize the the team in general and and those important parts of the team that you want to make sure that um, you build those up and make those a strong point of of what you're trying to do. Um, it's something that we really focused on, uh, this offseason. Um, and actually did a pretty good job of getting that done. I'm just talking from the D-line and the O-line perspective. So, um, it's something I believe in. Uh, it's something that, um, I think it's a foundation to every like winning football team is to make sure both O-line and D-line are stabilized. Um, it's something that we got to continue to look at. >> What about Parham? Um, >> Yep. >> obviously he doesn't have the experience with the unit where you talk about continuity, but >> what does he bring to the table and why did you target him? >> Yeah, well, the thing is he was with Geno before. And once you bring a new player inside, man, like it's important that he understands how those how the four guys operate. He's done that. Um, obviously when you come to this part, man, it's the mental part that we really try to focus on cuz the physical part we can't do anything about that when it comes to OTAs. So, we'll see exactly how it operates when it comes to training camp. >> Speaking of Geno, what has he done this spring to make an impression on you? >> Um, everything that I spoke about before. So, um, again, looking forward to seeing him grow. Um, especially with the pads on so we can see exactly um, how he can dominate inside. >> Does he similar to anyone you've seen over the years or remind you of anyone? he does. He does. Um, who was definitely dominant, you know, uh, in the middle of your defense. Um I thought special teams the guys had a really good understanding of that already. And the thing is we're steady building on that. You know, I don't want to give the give the give the people too much, but you know, I I do like what I see, you know, from the from those guys and it fired me up to make sure, you know, I'm doing my part, you know, so we're rushing collectively, you know, four four equals one, you know, and that and that's pretty much what we have to do. And just, you know, learning each other's rushing styles and play styles and stuff like that so we can go out there and it look like we've been playing together forever. You know. >> They clearly made it a priority to address the front seven and beef it up, you know, both in the draft and free agency and for you. I know you weren't here last year, but can you sense that you know, those guys, that entire unit has kind of beefed up a little bit and there's some new faces that are hungry ready to go out there and prove it. >> Uh I definitely again, there's a sense of urgency. And you know, I do like, you know, that uh we it's not about just bringing guys in. I feel like we we've brought the right guys in and um really it's just time on the grass together it would be exactly what we want it to be and most importantly what the organization wanted it to be. You know, so uh I do like uh what what has been done, you know, as far as the drive and even with me even being here free you know, free agency. I'm a happy camper. So, you know, I'm looking forward to the season. >> Can you take us through last off season and just how you came to the realization that like less is more for you? In terms of off season work and and just learning more about your body. So, many guys come into the league and it's like they have to really learn themselves. >> Mhm. I wouldn't say less is more. I think it's just um you know, uh cuz I'm working my tail off. It's not like I'm not, you know, training and stuff like that. >> I mean like some guys will run themselves into the ground in the off season. They're so hyper focused even guys at your position. By the time they come out here it's like they don't have anything left in the >> Yeah, it's just doing the right things, you know, everybody off season looks differently. Um as as you uh play in this league, you know, for a while you figure out what works for you and everybody's different and I understand and I know what works for me and uh you know, I appreciate the organization and the coaches, you know, respecting that and it's my job to make sure I do what I need to do to pay for it and I will. >> You were a teammate of Alex's Anzalone obviously. What What What are the Bucks getting in him in that inside linebacker role? >> So, uh Anzalone um we was drafted together in 2017. Um I've been around him for a while. Played with him last year two years in Detroit. Um smart, instinctive, tough, physical. Um I think he's what Not I think I know he's what every every team would want in a leader. You know, he is a leader and not only is he a great football player, he's a great person, you know, and his and he wants everybody to uh succeed and he understand that having body on everybody on the same page is important, especially on the defense. You know, he is the quarterback of the defense, essentially. So, um it's it's it's it's great. It's awesome. And, you know, behind closed doors, he's he's extremely funny, too. He's a funny guy. So, you know, it's it's great to actually, you know, have him here and be able to be on the same team um again with him. And, you know, I know exactly what he's going to bring to the table. And, uh I think uh we all be happy with the with the end result. >> You mentioned that a couple more seasons in Detroit was your best season. What did you learn most about yourself as an edge rusher, be it something technical or mental? And, how are you planning to apply that sort of thing to your game? >> Just knowing how to rush, just setting rushes up, you know, and it's it's pretty much it's just like it's like a chess game, you know, just knowing when to do certain things and just uh you know, again, setting up setting up your rushes within a defense. And then also um knowing the guys that's lined up beside you and just communicating effectively and, you know, not just out there doing your own thing. And, you know, that's just pretty much how you have success. And then also, you know, just great communication and feedback with the coaches on the sideline, you know, what you seeing and and and actually what I'm seeing on the field. And just having that open communication and being able to switch things up on the on the go uh throughout a game. You know, and I think that that's the difference between, you know, I think like first-year guys and guys that been on the grass, you be able to pick things up on the fly and then and adjust, you know, and also setting our rushes up, playing the game within the game. And that's pretty much all this is. It's uh you know, playing the game within the game. And, you know, you you eventually have some success. >> Yaya Diaby's kind of been a mainstay here as one of the edge rushers. What were your first impressions of seeing him on the field and then interacting with him? >> He's built like a machine. That's my friend. [laughter] Like when you see him, he's like, damn, wow, this this this dude this guy's a machine. But, um Yaya, I think he he's powerful. He's super powerful. Um smart football player. Love the game of football. And he's he's always uh you know, he's open to learn. And even me, you know, watching Baine and I watch different stuff. I'm always as a veteran guy, I'm open to learn new things and he's going to he's going to again, he's going to have a great year, too. Um you know, just just being curious and being open to learn new things and you know, we in meetings and I'm seeing how he see the game and I'm telling him how I how I see the game. And that's pretty much how you elevate, you know, year to year, you know, so I see some great things, you know, from him that he's done in the past and you know, he's already taking a step forward and getting better. So, you know, our room is is is stacked, you know, we got a we got a good room, a loaded room and a bunch of guys that's that want to get better and including myself. So, it's it's going to be great. >> Okay. Thank you. >> I appreciate it. >> Thank you. >> Appreciate it. >> All right, guys. Got Miles Killebrew. >> What's going guys? >> How much of a factor is Danny Smith in your >> I would say a giant factor. Um he he was my coach for a number of years in Pittsburgh. We have a pretty strong relationship. I know what he expects out there on the field. Um and so when he made the move down here, I you know, I I saw in my forecast sunny skies. I'll I'll say that. I'll say that. So, I'm excited to be here. I'm super pumped to get out on the field. Um obviously I'm on a limited capacity right now, which sucks. I hate it. Um but I can't I can't get out there. >> Will you be ready to go for training camp? >> That's the goal. Um, you know, I know they don't want me talking too much about injury right now, but um you know, had that significant knee injury last year and uh right now the timeline is to get rolling uh in training camp. That's the goal. >> I'm sure you saw Danny Smith in special teams and you guys out there winning some games in Pittsburgh. Can you just talk about how a play here or there can can can flip your loss into a win and >> Well, I'm a little biased. Um, I I love teams, always have. And uh I know how important it is. Danny talks all the time about uh the hidden yardage out there on the field. And so if we can get the ball, if we can get the drive started in a favorable position for for Baker, I know he's going to love it. I know if the defense has to pin an offense down in their own territory, they're going to love it. And so it's just a um it's a team win when your special teams is competing at a high level. >> Talk to you guys in the locker room. How much does it help for them even if you're not on the field to be able to kind of explain the game and how they to be like an extra >> Well, >> [snorts] >> don't say that too loud, extra coach. But um I think it is beneficial. You know, obviously I take it very serious. I I know how my bread is buttered, you know, I'm not here to be the franchise quarterback. I'm uh I'm here to play special teams, no doubt. And so I know the language that they speak, I can reiterate it. Danny's really big on multiple voices, same message. And so uh I know what I know what he's looking for. So it is helping. Uh but there's a number of very capable uh very smart uh players on this team, which I'm I'm really excited to play alongside. Um, you know, obviously you're very familiar with Cole Kief. You're um you're very familiar with uh Wisdom. These guys are I can go down the line. There's guys on this team that are are very smart, very good players and I'm really excited to get out on the field and play alongside with. >> When did you fall in love with with special teams? When did you realize that is where you're going to have your bread buttered? >> I mean, I a long time ago. I I got a scholarship to Southern Utah University because of my my kickoff film from high school. So it it goes way back. I um I take it very serious. My opinion, I think it's the purest form of the game. I think punt is the best play in the game, personally. I'm going to get a lot of laughs.
