I know that's when a lot of people go to the bathroom, you know, during the transitional periods, but I think it's I think it's critical. I take it very serious. I know that uh games can be won or lost on the back of special teams. So, I want to do everything I can in my part in my power to uh to benefit this awesome organization, get some wins. >> You're a special teams player, but what have you seen from the safety room and the guys there and then and then and then and then and the guys there and >> It's a great room. Uh Coach Dim has a really good environment there. Um obviously veteran leadership. I mean, you see the the billboards in the back, you know, the the guys on the billboards. There's There's some There's some very strong leadership in that room. Um if anything, I'm trying to add to uh you know, that veteran presence. I I know I've been playing for a long time, even if it has been primarily special teams. I still seen a lot of things. And so, uh just trying to make myself available in that regard, but it's a great room. I'm excited to be a part of it. What have I learned about Baker? Oh, he's awesome. He's a great guy, uh great ball player, uh real down-to-earth, approachable. And um I can see that the guys the offense rallies behind him. And uh he's a he's a winner. And so, it's it's exciting. I can't wait to see see more of him in camp. >> I was going to say guys on defense and offense said that, you know, he kind of elevates their intensity. Do you feel that on special teams as >> Oh, 100%. I um I think that uh I think the team is absolutely uh just littered with strong strong leadership. A lot of voices. Everyone's uh really excited. And it it feels like a winning culture. I'm excited to be a part of it. >> You were with Kenneth Gainwell last year at Pittsburgh. >> That's right. >> What stood out about about him? I mean, it's it's kind of unusual for a guy to come in and win the team MVP with That's right. with J.J. Watt, Cam Heywards, and a lot of Aaron Rodgers, a lot of stalwarts on that team. >> That's right. And he did. He was our MVP. And uh now he's here. He brings a lot to the table. He's a He's a tough tackle. And um you know, he's definitely going to help us win some games. Yep. Thanks, guys. >> All right. Appreciate it. Hey, maybe get out of this heat, huh?

title: Baker Mayfield: You Can Feel the Energy | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How we doing? >> How you feeling this new offense? >> Feel good. Um feel like we've made some really really good strides throughout the offseason. Um in terms of from day one install um with everybody just understanding the concepts of what we're really going to try and focus on. obviously new terminology um conceptually, you know, a lot of similar things that the guys that have been here have have seen and done, but terminology. So, you got to learn it. You got to treat the like it's day one install. You're learning a whole new program for the first time. So, I I think we've we've come a long way. There's still a lot of work to be done, but um yeah, I I think the vets have grasped it and really taken ownership of it, and I think the young guys are kind of following suit with that. And so, it's been good to see. Um, yeah, first day of mini camp here and got two more days to to really continue to iron it out. >> What are your thoughts on on Ted Hurst, the new receiver? >> Really like Ted's game. Um, somebody that, you know, he's a big bigger body receiver. Uh, exceptional hands. I think his body control, he can really cover a lot of ground. I think for a big guy can cover a lot of ground. And so, uh, he should be a weapon for us. He should be able to help us out. And for him, it's, you know, the the rookie the normal rookie stuff, learning the offense formations to where it's not he's not having to think the whole time. It's more second nature and and that goes with the whole time. But he'll get better each day and continue to grasp it and and help us out. >> This camp feel any different, Baker, in terms of energy. >> Yeah, there's definitely a lot more energy, I think. And it's when you lose guys that have been here for a long time. Um like Levante and Mike and Dean and just others. Uh forget a few names, but people kind of wait around and wait for those guys to make a play or say something. And when you get new faces and obviously Nacho's been here before, you get guys to come in and spark a new energy. Uh maybe it's trash talk or just the way they approach the game, it's it uplifts everybody. And so it's been really fun to see. Um, obviously all the new pieces on defense that that in itself brings a lot of energy and so it's made every single practice competitive. Um, obviously we had a had a day taken away just but that's that's the type of energy and uh, you know, competition that we're having right now which is really good for for the Bucks. >> You got a new toy in game too, right? >> Yeah, Kenneth has been doing great. You know, somebody that I've respected from afar when he was with Philly and with the Steelers. Um, just you can tell he's a sharp kid. uh that's always been able to do pass protection stuff. He he was doing that in Philly from from a very early on his career point and uh then in Pittsburgh absolutely balled out and now to have him here we're lucky he's extremely sharp leader uh can do everything he asked for and obviously with Bucky you know coming back slowly it's it's good to have those guys and obviously the running back room is still having Tuck in there as well. talked about how talent obviously for you as a quarterback you know everything would run through 13 is it it's obviously going to be different but is it better in some ways does somebody have to emerge as that number one or how does that work >> you know yeah it's different it'll be it'll be different without Mike and that's teams would have to double cover him or bring a safety over the top cloud coverage and u so it'll be different but that also I think based on personnel and moving guys our receivers are all somewhat similar skill sets. Some guys do a little bit different things better than others, but um we'll be able to kind of dictate based on personnel on those guys, moving them around and really seeing what defenses are, how they're going to try and cover us, attack us, and so um it's it's a great luxury to have. Um but yeah, we expect all those guys, I mean, I think Chris looks really really good right now. um just training with him the whole offseason and J-Mack as well just those guys have busted their tails and so Chris looks like he's back into his pure form. Um J-Max's healthy. uh you know he looked looked great at this point last year unfortunately got hurt and then obviously a mecha taking those steps from year one to year two and TZ obviously showed flashes last year and then Ted Hurst and um you know Cade Payne Bower Co Dev I mean we we got some weapons and so it's it's a luxury to have but for me it's going through my reads not trying to force it because with with the system that we have and the guys we have somebody should be open. The last time we talked to you, you were at your camp and you talked about the fact that you and the team were pretty far apart on contract negotiations. I don't know if anything has progressed since we last talked to you and um how much does that kind of linger in the back of your mind while you're out here practicing and then as you go into? >> Uh no, pretty much the same. But for me, like I told you guys, it's not going to affect how I approach this. Um things will happen when they should, but for now I'm worried about getting better each day, finishing mini camp and this offseason program the right way and uh going into going into training camp. So yeah, just handle it one day at a time. >> Any indication to you about, you know, during these negotiations about the need to to protect your body even more? I mean, I know it's a challenge. >> I've started every single game last year for the three years, so I don't know if that should ever be a question. >> Baker, you've gone to war with Alex Analone in New Orleans and then also now he's a teammate, but also last year in Detroit. What are your thoughts on on his game and what he can help bring to his defense? >> Yeah. Um, I think first and foremost, it physically he's a great player, but I I think with his experience and being in different systems and bouncing around, I think his recognition of of of scheme and just communication style, having to play with different teams, uh, it's you can tell he's he's really really good at it. Getting guys on the same page. um he's he's out there kind of messing with me, making some dummy calls and obviously for for him to do that, he's got to have his guys on the same page with him and uh so it's it's fun to do that. It's like a it's like a chess game out there and u makes it really fun and and competitive at practice, but he's going to help us out tremendously. Um yeah, so I'm excited about it. >> Also, Asan Robinson brings a different presence to the defense. >> Yep. Uh yeah, he's uh I think I think people have said it. we needed some over there and he's one of those. I'm pretty happy I'm not having to go up against him anymore. Um yeah, he just he he sets a tone in different manner, you know. He's not he's not the loudest person by any means, but he brings a phys physical presence. Um you can kind of see it stamped on his forehead. He's ready to compete and fight wherever. What were some of the things that you're focusing on the quarterback position? >> Uh footwork I think um you know towards the last half of the year last year. You know obviously injuries always play a part for me but um really staying consistent with my footwork. I think there were things that you know I kind of lost track of some of that during the last half of the year. And so and Chandler's really good at it. Chandler Whitmer uh has really been honing in on it. at times it can be pretty pretty annoying how meticulous he is about it but for me I love that it's I want to be coached hard and I think he's doing an incredible jobs yeah so first and foremost footwork in this system is is all based on footwork the timing of the routes concepts so if I'm on time good things will happen especially with the weapons we have >> the next time we'll be able to talk with you the the quarterback series is going to come out and breaks I know that earlier in your time here I think you declined the opportunity to do the show what was what went into the decision making to say yeah I'll do it and B, what do you hope that people learn about you along the way and they kind of get to see every part of you on and off the field? >> Yeah, I think turning it down the first few times, I think for me was it seems like it's a me me thing and I wanted to make sure it wasn't going to be like that. So, talking to guys that have done it in the past, I mean, continuous conversations with Payton Manning about it's really not that invasive. you know, somebody's going to be miked up on a game day anyway once a week during practice and uh just for me couple of sitdown interviews outside of the building and capturing some family footage. So, uh I wanted to get a lot of that stuff captured just as the phase of life that we're going through right now in the next the next chapter of the journey for us. Um but also I think I do it to myself, but people have a persona or an idea about who I am until you really get to know me, which is fine. And so I hope that gives an insight to the fact that uh I truly love this game. I love my teammates and I I bust my ass. >> How much did you feel like you needed to be? Because you talked about it a lot with us. You know, the Bucks have allowed you to be myself. >> Being in that type of environment. I mean, like I'd imagine that allows you to be in a position where you feel like you can let down your guard and allow >> Oh, absolutely. Uh, I mean, anytime you feel comfortable enough and it's been open and honest communication from the get-go since I've been here and so anytime you feel like that, uh, and they they know that all I want to do is win. So, as long as that wasn't going to be a distraction, as long as it wasn't going to take away from the real goals at hand, uh, it was going to be okay and that they made sure of that. >> Exactly. Yeah, it's been great. >> We talked to Cody a couple weeks ago. He was just so happy to be back out there. >> Yeah. >> For all your guys to just be healthy right now and be out there. Um, great. You know, I said it time and time again. I think when those five guys are healthy, it's the best unit in the league. Um, you know, unfortunately, they didn't take one single snap together last year, and that that that'll affect your play. It's too hard to win in this league without your big boys. But on the other side of it, it gave a lot of guys some experience and some reps. They were thrown into there. So, you're looking at it, we have a great group up front, but we also have guys that have had experience and been thrown in the fire. So, depthwise, I feel really good about it. you know, it's the course of the season, somebody's going to get banged up. You're going to have to have people sub in and do that. But I I think we're prepared for that. And I think the guys are hungry just to get back out there and and take control of the game because they know how good they are when they're all rolling. >> What' you learn about yourself, Baker, when uh team kind of went off the rails after >> um that I still hate losing more than I love winning. I think that was that was the most frustrating thing is, you know, some of those games that we had won based on the little details late in games early in the season that we weren't doing the same things in the back half of the year. And whether that's attention to detail, not taking each meeting install for granted and making sure that no matter what point of the season is, you're overcommunicating. Especially with different guys in there, making sure you're talking about the little details of the timing like, "Hey, you have to be at this point right now. You got to be open. you're number one in the read or you're hey you're last in the read you can take your time you can kind of mess with the you know your release and whatnot so just overcommunicating some of the conceptual things but um I I learned that no matter what I was I was fighting through a lot but I was trying to be the same same person for these guys each and every day and that's to me that's what a good leader does >> feel like you tried to do too much at times >> no I mean I think there were I think there were times that you know um trying to force the ball in certain situations you know there's a lot of throws I want back don't get me wrong on that uh in the in the flow of the game, you know, it's you have to react. You have to trigger it. And I've always played like that. And you know, last year some of those plays didn't go my way. Um but yeah, moving forward, it's still got to be consistent for these guys each and every day. Uh and let the big boys handle it up front and and roll from there. I feel really confident about where our defense is at instead of trying to, you know, have to put up 30 each game. I feel confident that we're going to have a really good team. and having that lineback intact, >> can you get back to that 24 running game? >> Yeah, huge key for you guys to win. >> Yeah, I think so. I I think um you know, this is not to downplay Josh Gard whatsoever because I I love Grizz. Um but I think Zach with his understanding and history of the run game and obviously his relationship with Liam and him talking to those guys about, you know, the the things that these guys are really good at and obviously he's learning it. He's he's seen it firsthand. And so I think that's going to help us out. It's, you know, it used to say that the offense runs through Mike, but it it even in 24 it still ran through the run game and that opened a lot of things up for us. So, uh, guys know that you can't just sit back there and drop back 50 times a game. That's not a that's not a recipe for success in this league. So, uh, they understand that it's a physical game that we have to we have to be that way. >> Speaking of the running game, Sean Tucker's one of those guys that had to step up last year and play a lot was >> Led your team in rushing touchdowns. What did you see from from him in terms of growth last year and how he played that year? Yeah, I I think obviously we've all kind of known about his speed the whole time, the the explosive play potential and I think for him to take those steps and uh just take advantage of his skill set and we saw that last year and just growth within the concepts, understanding that as a back you're supposed to have your eyes and and read the linebackers, whatever the guy over the tackle on certain concepts. And I think he was really focusing on the details of that, like, okay, where am I supposed to be looking at here for the the read on the run? And then I think the biggest thing I've seen this offseason is uh improvement in the hands. I think he's catching the ball really well right now and that's that's something that obviously Kenneth and Bucky do extremely well. So I think Tuck has taken the next step for that that um we can utilize those guys as everywhere on the field as weapons. Thank you.

title: Todd Bowles on Start of Minicamp: Ted Hurst III's Role | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: afternoon. >> Thoughts on practice today? What you like? >> Uh, I think they're getting the schemes down on both sides. That's important. We're starting to understand situational football a little better. We just got to keep working on that. So, that's really the basis of it. >> No, he is not. >> You haven't seen Christian Roseboom out here. Was he missing today's >> He's excused. He has a personal thing that he has to handle. But he he'll be here. >> He's excused. >> Will he be here tomorrow? >> No, he won't be here for this mini camp, but he'll be at training camp. >> Why is he going to have to put his >> Well, we're just bringing him in that late. He's full speed. He needs to go uh come training camp, but we don't need to see him right now. >> How the goal line work there? Did you get more from the the windfield interception or the three touchs down there? >> Don't get anything from it. It's hard to do goal line when you're not hitting people and you're not covering people like that. So, it's just about executing the mechanics for us. >> How has Josh Hayes looked as a quarterback? I know he's been a special teams ace for you, but how's his development been on defense? >> He's got the skill set. Just got to be more consistent in small things and he's working on that this year, but he's made great strides this spring. Seems like every practice power does something a play here and there. Just your thoughts on how he's coming along. >> He's working, you know, like the rest of the tight ends. He's working. He looks like a good athlete out there in shorts and t-shirt. Get the pads on. We get a better feel. >> A bunch of corners and tight ends. Do they none of the guys that are held out right now have anything over? >> Not at this time. No. >> Coach, this is the first time for us to see Mohamd out here and also for you. How do you think about him first day mini camp? Again, just getting the kinks out. We know he's in great shape. We just gave him a couple reps here and there. Just working on individual, but he's up on the scheme because he's been in all the meetings. Just got to continue getting them reps. >> What impresses you most about Ruben Bane on the field from what you've seen this offseason? >> For me, it's probably his intelligence. Just his understanding of the game. You know, some some things you can't teach that. He doesn't learn the game like a normal rookie. He does natural things that a three or four year guy can do and, you know, that's good to see. What are your thoughts on uh Zack Robinson, his new OC execution out here? The fact the guys are not making a whole lot of mental errors. How's execution? >> He's a stickler for execution. I really like that about him. A stickler for detail. He he has a something he's trying to get done every day. Whatever they're trying to get done, be it in the run game or the pass game or the screen game, whether it's the blocking, whether it's the technique, whether it's working on turnovers, he's very deliberate on the things that he's trying to do and the guys are buying in. How's Baker's performance been throughout the OTAAS and today's mini camp? >> I think it's learning for everybody. You know, Baker's learning too is still some of the offense is old, but a lot of the offense is new. So, his performance has been great. He's a good leader. He understands the game. He knows where to go with the ball. He's getting everybody on the same page. >> Todd, what's the biggest difference between this year and last year with Ted Johnson? >> Just a year under his belt mentally understanding what to do, not running around like a chicken with his head cut off so early. You know, he had to learn a bunch of positions and injuries forced him into playing real fast. So, that kind of threw him in the fire. Although he performed well, mentally it slowed down for him. >> He looks a little bigger and stronger. Put on a little weight. >> He's probably up to 125 right now. >> How about David Walker? He kind of had a medical red shirt year last year getting hurt so early in training camp, but he's been out here with the brace. How does he perform? >> The last two practices look like more the David Walker we've seen when we drafted. He looks a lot healthier. He's moving a lot freely, not thinking about his knee, and he's starting to see the speed and the athleticism that he had last year. So, he's just got to keep working at it. >> Daniel's got a lot of reps in the rookie camp, obviously. >> I'm sorry, who was that? >> Daniel. >> Okay. >> A lot of reps in rookie camp. How has he progressed to this point? >> It's slowing down for him. You know, that's a lot for a rookie quarterback coming in then seeing all the looks he's seeing on defense. The game is really slowing down for him. Energetic, bright kid every day. I'm really interested to see him in camp. What are you looking to see out of Baker, especially in this new system over the next few days? >> Just continuing to get very good at all the little things, just understanding the offense by himself so he can take it over, which he's doing a very good job at, but to continue to do that, it'll be good. >> Todd, you could have four or five new defensive starters week one. How would that how does that affect you at all in terms of tweaking the scheme that you've been used to, trying to adjust the scheme to the personnel? I think it tweaks every year. It's tweaking some now. We're getting to see some of the strengths of those guys to where we have to tweak the scheme. It'll be more in pads. Uh I think you adjust it to how they play without hurting anybody else. And you know, I think it's a good thing for our system because some of it needs to change. >> Have you done that kind of thing before? >> We have been back for a couple weeks now. Just your thoughts on on how he's moving along. >> He's moving well and he's running well. You know, look forward to seeing him in training camp. Todd, picking up on what I was saying, do the new pieces that you have on defense to the drafting free agency allow you to do more than maybe you have in in the past or are they just maybe even better fits for what you already like to do and in the plays that you play? >> I think they all have their specialty. You know, it's not about what I like to do, it's about what they can do. You know, we try to tailor and see that. Some things are surprising us a little bit by what they can do. Other things we try to stay away from which we think they can't do but all of them bring their pluses in. It's just a matter of matching those with the guys that are already here and then bringing that all together. >> You think with with Bane and Mohamad and a healthy campy that get a lot of pressure with just four and >> that is our hope. Yes. >> What does Mohamd bring to this this defense and you know what was it like seeing him out here today with everybody? >> He brings a lot of depth to that position more than we've had in quite a while. Obviously with Bane and Muhamd and Yaya and Nelly and Brad and David Walker coming back and the other young guys that we have here. We hadn't had that kind of depth in a long time. So they're really pushing each other. So it should be good. It should be fun to see in camp. >> What's your comfort level with Ted Hurst and you envision him helping you right away? >> Uh that's a work in progress right now. He's a very bright guy, but every rookiey's got some learning to do and that that'll progress through the preseason, probably through the regular season as well. But I do see him helping us right away. >> How you feeling about the depth of corner? Uh would you like a veteran presence in the mix? >> I would like to see those guys get healthy and go through the summer a little bit and then I'll determine whether we need a veteran or not once I get a look at those guys. >> T with Baker being on the the upcoming series at quarterback during the offseason, are you going to watch that uh when when it comes out before training camp? If it's not past my bedtime and vacationwise, I usually don't watch football when I'm on vacation, but I'll eventually see it. Yes, I will eventually see it. >> Can you speak to watch it on the plane? >> I I sleep well on planes. >> Lucky, can you speak to to Danny Smith and what you've been able to accomplish from a special team standpoint? >> Very energetic. He keeps everyone engaged. Starters, backups, coaches, everyone alike. Um, like the work he's putting in right now. Obviously, the meetings have been great. When we get the pads on at full speed, we like to see those guys execute his plan. Thank you. Thanks,

title: Carnell Tate, Alontae Taylor and Solomon Thomas Speak After Titans Minicamp
text: you going to be at the end of tomorrow than you were when you arrived here? >> Um, it's just a matter of how more comfortable I am. I just felt like I was more uncomfortable like since the first day. It just unlearning a bunch of things I learned from college and relearning the new offense and new system here. >> Brian Dable, he said despite doing this for a long time, you're one of the best guys at picking things up and we see you moving across the formation and everything. What's been the key for you to play all these positions but still play as smoothly and as fast as you? Um, it started with coach Hartline um at Ohio State. He made it a priority for me to learn all the different receiver groups because the more you understand what each position has, the more you understand the playbook. So, it was just nothing new. Just coming over here like the more positions you know, the more you know understand the playbook and that way you you're able to play different positions. >> What's feedback encouragement been like I guess from teammates as they've seen you out here and seen you have some success? It's been pretty much just keep keep balling, keep making play, just keep being yourself. And then I'll just try to pick Wandell and uh all the other guys, Wendell, uh DK, E and then Red about how how I can be better and then what they can see and what would they do differently? >> How helpful has Wandell been given his experience in the offense? Has helped shorten the learning curve for you guys? >> Yeah, Wendell has been a tremendous help for me. Uh especially I go out there some plays and blank and then Wendell helped me because he knows what everyone has cuz he's been with Dable for the past four or five years. trying to talk us through the wide variety of option routes in this whole deal. Is there one or two variations of that that are particularly difficult to learn or execute for you coming into the league? >> Um, no. I don't really think it's nothing. Um, it's just a matter of how fast you can go out there and play and uh understand the offense. >> Did you surprise yourself at all with how quick or smooth the transition has been making all the highlight plays this early? >> Uh, no, I didn't surprise myself at all. At the end of the day, just football. Just going out there and doing what I do best. We're receivers. We get paid to catch the ball. So, >> how have you seen the connection between you and Camro over the last few weeks? >> Oh, man. Came on D. We go kick it, go hang out in his crib. We talk stuff to each other. We make each other better and then we always see on the same page at the end of plays. >> What do you do between time champions and uh come back for training camp? Um, just a matter of taking care of my body, getting ready for training camp, staying in shape, and then just ultimately building that connection with the receivers and ultimately can you'll hear a lot of guys when they get picked high in the draft talk about like there's a lot to live up to when they come in. What's your thoughts on that in terms of what you expect from yourself? >> Uh, perfectly comes from doing good things all the time. So, I mean, I'm used to it. I played at Ohio State. I played at the highest level. So, I'm just going to go out there, continue to be who I am, and just go play football at the highest level. How much you relish maybe being able to beat a DB who can run with you with route craft and nuance and and that kind of stuff? >> A lot. I mean, at the end of the day, receivers, you're not always going to be butt naked open. So, it's just a matter of how do you can separate at the top of your route and make go out there and make a play. >> Is that a normal phrase that receivers use? >> Uh, yeah. [laughter] >> Cam says he never compliments himself. Is that kind of a motto that you take as well or you let yourself kind of relish in some of those moments? >> Um, no. I don't really compliment myself. I let the others speak for me and I just always try to be better because no matter how good I do, however great of a play I make, I always can find a way to be better in that play within that play. >> Do you feel like you and Cam have pretty similar personalities? It seems by the way you guys are talking that you think kind of the same way. >> Uh, I mean, I don't know. I haven't really been around Cam that much, but I don't know. We just two competitive people like that that wants to see uh each other do great things. You guys are competing, but what are the DBs on this team? What's the interaction like with them? Whether it's out here on the field or maybe in the locker room to try to help you get better. >> Tell my Tay my locker room mate. So me and Tay chop it up whenever he comes in. We laugh, we joke, I ask him questions about being he's a obviously, so I just ask him things about my rookie experience. So yeah. And then on the field, we we laugh, we talk crap to each other, we just make each other better. >> This time of year, what what's defined progress for you, would you say? >> Just understanding the playbook for real. I mean, that's the biggest thing right now. Just focus on understanding the playbook and go out there just catching the ball consistently. >> How how much time do you spend with it in a in an average day? How much will you spend with it during your time away? >> Spend with what? >> With the playbook. >> All day. I mean, the more you know, the better it is for you. That way, you're not out there thinking that you don't know nothing. So, the more I study, the more confidence I am in my game. And then that allows me to go play fast. >> Good. >> Have you seen yourself get more acclimated in Nashville? and have you done anything exploring wise? >> Um, yeah, I'll be seeing myself get more acclimated. I'm just trying to focus on just find a different sport by extend my variety of food and try not to be so picky. [laughter] >> Thanks, Carter. Thank you all tonight. >> Uh, it's great. Um, we got a, you know, really good offense, young quarterback, um, few veteran receivers, few young receivers, everybody competing. Um, I think secondary wise, you know, we're improving, we're getting better. Um, you know, we're facing a challenge every day. Monte, how do you do this? You guys obviously you guys have put a lot in over the last several several times, but yet it's now training camp. What do you want to see this team get out of these couple days? >> Really, man? Just just finish um you know, just um you know, being in the playbook. Uh let's work on not having any mental errors. Uh being where we're supposed to be. Um but most importantly, just competing. Uh you know, we go tomorrow and then we got a long break. So I think throughout that time, you you know, you hone in on your craft. you work on things that you feel like you need to improve on. Um, ask your coaches, you know, where they think that you should be better at. Um, and you work on that in the offseason. So, right now, just, you know, work on the playbook and just compete. >> How much of a sense you guys in the secondary have for the offense's option routes and what they're trying to do? >> One more time. routes and what they're trying to do for to you, what they're trying to read. >> Yeah. Um, I mean, I feel like, you know, as a secondary, you just win your leverage. Um, react to everything else. Um, you know, right now we we got certain calls. Um, you just got to do your job. Um, and then just compete. I feel like, you know, some of some of us older guys, we kind of have a good idea. Um, and just kind of giving the younger guys a few tips to uh, help them be um, you know, a little quicker uh, in certain directions. >> How are you coming along as far as getting reaclimated to being out there on the island on the outside? >> Yeah. Um, you know, every offseason I train as a corner. Um, I always implement a few things as far as like nickel work. Um, but you know, I feel like I'm at home. I'm right where I want to be. Um, and so, uh, you know, nothing new, nothing different. Um, like I said, I've been training as a corner this whole time throughout my career. So, I'm very comfortable. >> I saw you bump inside maybe one or two reps, you know, as like a nickel. Is that something that >> today? >> No, through throughout this process. There was one I want to say a Tuesday in OTAAS you did, but um is is that something that that you asked to do or is that something you would like to do or you just kind of going with the program? How how is that? >> Yeah. Um I feel like, you know, I know I know what they want from me. I know where they want me to be. Um and that's an outside corner. Um and so, you know, that's where I'm at. That's where I'm honing in on. Um obviously learning the whole playbook, right? So that, you know, I know where my help's at. I know where Marcus is. Um so, you know, I'm a corner and that's where they want me to be. So that's where I'm going to be at. What what's your impression of some of the guys around you in the defense and maybe just the culture in the building since you've been here? >> Great group of guys, man. Um, our D line's nasty. Um, our our edges are dope. Our linebackers are very communicative. Um, very good competitors. Um, safeties are dope, man. I feel like we have a really good defense. I think Coach Solid's done a great job with bringing the right guys into [clears throat] the building. Um, and I think it's just going to continue to get better as we build chemistry with one another. Um, and we continue to compete with one another. What's your early scout report on Tate and just kind of what are the keys to trying to slow him down? >> Um he's polished, man. Uh for for a rookie to come in, um doing some of the things that he's doing is really really exciting. Um you know, I just continue to compete with him, continue to push him to, um you know, polish him in certain areas as well. Um you know, come Sundays, uh he's going to be very exciting to watch. >> You said you feel at home out of corner. What What's the biggest challenge on the outside playing that position? >> I think just being on an island. Um, I think I mean some people speak differently. I think the inside's a little bit more difficult than being on the outside. There's so much space when you're in a slot. Um, but on the outside, you get out of the sideline. Um, and I think if you just went to your leverage and you just be patient, play the technique. Um, you give yourself the best opportunity to be successful. >> As a mental convert, if you will, what do what do you think of Marcus from what you've seen of him so far? >> Yeah, Marcus is doing good, man. Um, a guy who's in the playbook. Uh, a guy who meets with his coach all the time. Um, a a young promising player. um a guy who owns in onto his position. Um and I'm super excited to work beside him. Um but just just to love the fact that he's willing to learn, he's willing to listen. >> How has it been being back at home to feel settled in and will you be here for the rest of the summer? >> Yeah. Um super excited to be home. Um my fiance and my daughter, they finally moved in and um you know, it's super exciting knowing that we can just go down the road to see my mom. I just bought her a home um in Murphy'sboro and so uh it feels good. my family doesn't have to drive seven hours to come see me play. Um I can just come up and down the road. So um I love it. I'm glad to be back. Um and yeah, I'll be here throughout the summer. >> Any big plans for Fourth of July? >> Uh yeah. So me, my fiance, a little bit of some of her family going to St. Thomas um enjoy a little getaway um and just kind of decompress a little bit and then come back and get ready to work. >> Was the home for your mom a surprise or is that something you've been wanting to do for a long time? How'd that unfold? >> Yeah, I've always wanted to do it. Um, obviously could have done in my rookie contract. Um, but I wanted to get them something that I feel like they really loved. Um, and so I just waited till this deal came through and um, moved on it pretty fast. Um, they loved it. It was their dream home. They had no idea. Um, and I think, you know, being in this position, the most cool thing to do is get moms a home um, and be able to take care of your family. >> As you've been settling into this defense, you look around, what do you like about the the possibilities that have been assembled on the defensive line? Um, I just like the talent on our roster. You know, you got Jeffrey Simmons, John Franklin Myers, um, Jake Martin, Jermaine Johnson, all guys who um, I played with a bunch of those guys before and they they played at all pro level, great rushers, but also great teammates. They play with high effort. Um, they're very coachable and they're great leaders. So, um, just the talent on the on the defensive line has impressed me and I'm excited to play with these guys. Um, start camp, mesh together, and, uh, you know, have a great season. watching you guys work with Aaron White Cotton and some guys before practice with Tenzel Smart. There's such a focus on technique and it's seems like it's transferring into practice. How much do you like having such useful things to do in individual period? What are your thoughts on working with that? >> Yeah. Um I've been with Coach White about seven years out of my 10 year career. He's been um amazing. You know, I'm surprised he isn't a DC or head coach yet. And you know, he's just given so much to us. he uh he is so good at giving back to his players and and being so intense and the reason he can be so intense and be so hard on us is because he shows that he cares and then Tanzo Smart I play with him um for four years of my career and like he's one of my best friends and so it's crazy to see him in the coaching role but it's been really cool this year to see him find his voice and he's really finding it. He's jelling with the guys and you know he takes drills to action and so that's really really cool to see the drills get on the field and and see them uh pay off. But, uh, you know, we have a great coaching duo and, um, all the players are enjoying the coaches right now. So, it's been good. >> You've been in solid system before where he runs people in in waves and rotates pretty rapidly. How is how is that different and how how can it be more effective than regular rotations where the starters take the vast majority and the backups just spell them occasionally? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, we all stay fresh and, you know, we you want to rush fresh. you want to, you know, be in there and and be able to dominate. But, you know, coach Wcon, coach Salah, they're still going to play, you know, the guys who are are the best players, like Jeff and all those guys, like they're still going to be on the field the most. Like, yeah, we're going to rotate. We're going to be fresh, but there's like the guys who were out there, like Jeff and them, they're still going to get majority of the reps, but we have a lot of talent to back them up and come in and and come fresh and give Jeff a break. Give him three, four plays. Jeff comes back in fresh, balling out. So, you know, it's a good system. It's it's good. That's why we have so many guys on the D line and we keep so many on the roster so we can have that rotation and keep the guys fresh. >> Those lines just said when asked about the defense, you started by saying our D line is nasty. How much do you guys take it upon yourselves to really set the tone for what this team could be? >> Yeah. I mean, it's it's just a way of our life. Like our our our way of life in the trenches is like you have to be violent, you have to be nasty, you have to have a certain type of mentality to play this game. Like there's not a defensive lineman that I don't know in the in the world that's not somewhat crazy, you know, to to to line up every every play and hit someone in the head and and use your hands in a violent way. Like that's that's the only way you can play play this position and and it's something that coach Whitecon preaches every day every year I've been with him and it's just something that a defensive lineman lives by in his life. >> I imagine coming out you you envisioned a 10-year career on the edge. Can you talk us through kind of your transition to to being more of an inside guy and what that's been like physically and mentally? >> Yeah. No, I um actually the opposite. I I imagine coming in as an interior player, I I played maybe 15 plays on the edge in college. I played a four eye. I don't consider that the edge. So, I I thought coming in the coming the league I would play kind of that hybrid detackle position. You know, more of a three tech, sometimes five, you know, kind of within that range. And then like you know things things were different. I was on a defensive line where guys were better than me. You had Eric Armstead, DeForest Buckner inside. Like those guys had the right to play. So I had to find myself in a different position, learn from it, uh adjust, adapt and just find my place in the league. Around my fourth year, I came inside um back where I was comfortable and you know started finding my way and started getting in the groove. Um and you know just you know feel very blessed to be entering my 10th year. That's something I don't take lightly but uh you know I still have a lot of work to do. What do you do year 10 different from when you first came in league as far as preparing for the season? Whether it's now or during these weeks leading up to camp? >> Yeah. Uh definitely a lot of mental and physical preparation. You know, making sure I reset my mind, you know, uh come into the season fresh, not burnt out, not stressed, not not worried about this and that. Making sure I come in prepared mentally, but also physically, you know, making sure I'm peing at the right time. You know, it's a long offseason. You know, I train from late January to July and then when the season starts. So, I can't just go 100% every single day and then enter the season burnt out. You know, I have to program correctly. That's why I have a a team that I do in Dallas back at home, Mason and Scott, you know, they get me right every offseason. And, um, you know, it's just a lot of lot of more mental preparation on the side of things going into year 10. Just things I've learned from vets along the way. But, uh, you know, it's been a great ride and thankful for all my vets who have taught me a lot of things. You mentioned the mental preparation [laughter] this June being men's mental health month. Can you just speak to the importance of having an understanding of how that could impact cuz I know that impact you personally. >> Yeah. Um yeah know u mental health is something that's huge for me you know uh have a have a foundation with my family um have been impacted by it uh personally lost my sister to suicide and went through my own struggles. Um but mental health is something that's inevitable for everyone in the world especially men. you know, we all think we're tough and we're just going to, you know, push through it, but it's it catches up with us some days. Like, as men, it's important to understand we're emotional human beings that we can cry, we can go get help, we can seek therapy, we can seek uh safe places with other men to talk about the struggles that we have going on. Um, we're losing way too many men in the world to suicide, and we're losing way too many people in the world to suicide. Um, you know, we've lost way too many many people. Appreciate you. Way way too many people in the NFL to suicide. Especially this past year, I lost my teammate Marshon Neland. May God rest his soul and be with Catalina and um Rond Del Moore and Ka Lacy. You know, there's there's it's it's right in front of us, but we still have guys to find to thinking that men don't go through mental health. It's been in front of us. The statistics are there. Men die at two or three times the rate as women. And you know, if we don't start talking about it, these things will keep happening. So, we have to have the conversation. We have to let men know it's okay to cry. It's okay to be emotional. It's okay to go to therapy cuz it's the most preventable death. But we refuse to talk about it cuz we think this masculinity thing keeps us away from being emotional. No, men are emotional human beings. Men have feelings. Men can go through all that and still be strong and tough. It's it's takes way more strength to be vulnerable and go get help and tell someone how you're really feeling than it takes to be quiet and be like, "Oh, I'm a tough guy cuz I'm quiet." Silence does not equal strong. So, >> as someone who's spent time with Saul in the past, what is it about him and his approach that is able to get the best out of defensive line and the defense in general? >> Yeah, I would say uh Saul is very intense. Like, he doesn't yell a lot, but he's very intense. Like, he he has hard practices. He pushes us really hard. Um, but he's all about the small processes pro process steps to becoming great. and you know just taking them from the first day in April to telling us you know our saying is own the south and then just taking that and you know the small steps of individual taking them to to a team taking them to competition and so it's just a whole culmination of um his approach to the process but um I just love how intense he is because that brings that brings the violence out. He's a big health guy, big fitness guy, big military guy and you know he brings that into football as well which is cool. Is there something specifically you see different in him today than maybe you saw in prior stops? >> Yeah, I mean um you know I was with him in New York and his first time being a head coach and um you know I think Solid did a great job given everything that we had going on there and you know I don't think the way things ended there were fair in any way. I don't I don't think life is fair. I don't think this game is fair but the way things ended weren't right and um to see him have his confidence back and that swagger about him back is is awesome. and he's back to the solo I knew in in San Fran with that swagger with that intensity and passion and um I'm really happy for him and I'm happy to be back playing for him. >> Thanks

title: Cam Ward Talks Titans Minicamp, Training Camp Prep and Building Chemistry
text: How is the program up until until this week? >> Oh, it's been great. Coach Davis is starting the system from the whole offense. I think the the position that's been leading us the most has been the old line. Those guys have been bringing it each and every day. With Slaton up front leading the charge, he's been great. So, just keying off them then me and my seven receivers getting our timing and making plays. >> How much better do you feel like the timing's gotten in the off season program from when you started? >> Oh, way better. Especially the more reps that we get with each other instead of just trying to limit people out on certain reps. And that's going to be something that we continue to get over the summer when we off. Then just continue to get them in training camp. >> Picking up on that, Dayball was talking about option routes. How how far along you feel you guys are with that and how how super in sync you guys have to be when when when the season rolls around on those to make this offense work? >> Um just depends on the route runner, depends on which option route it is. And just the the timing and space that I have for that route and the receiver has. So, that's just going to come with getting different looks as we go through practice and training camp. Then also when we're off time just trying to simulate certain coverages and try to put the ball in a specific area that I want to put it. >> Yeah, you you you think that is a good way to to work an offense? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. It's not just option routes we do everything. There's going to be a lot of stuff that no one in the NFL does but us. But, you know, we're going to be efficient at it, we're going to be effective at it, and we're going to do what we need to do to win games. >> As you continue to get out here and get more throws in, how is the shoulder feeling and how are you doing as far as getting the mechanics, the footwork, and everything that you've been working on with with DC and them? >> Uh real good. Especially just from an endurance standpoint, that was the biggest key for me because I'm just so used to going going going. Then when you have to sit back for a while then get your body going, you got to stay in that routine of routine of keep going and getting the reps with your guys that way when you come back in training camp, um there's no hiccups. We should start camp how we finishing this up, um good, and just be prepared for the season. >> Do you have any soreness or anything like that in in the shoulders? It's pretty good. >> No, good. Yep. >> Cam, how have you worked on improving your accuracy and ball placement this off season from where you were last year, and how are you continuing to do that going forward? >> Uh I just continue to focus on fundamentals, um whether that's feet, arm, everything to being a quarterback. Um and then having, you know, myself be accurate in certain coverages and the receiver, you know, feeling which way I'm trying to turn his body and stop him if I need to versus certain coverage. Um so, getting that relationship of spatial awareness um within the offense, I think that'll help out everybody. >> Coaches have attributed your improvement enough from last year to this year? I think it has to be a factor. Um I think it's more of just consistency on both sides, uh whether my side or the or the receiver side, and make sure we're seeing the same things on the field with the same things on film as well. >> Coaches have attributed a lot of your misses to new system, new guys, all of that. Which coach? Both Robert and Brian. Do Do you think that's that's fair, or have there been some that are are plays that you should be making regardless of whether stuff is is new or different? >> Nah, just think it depends on the situation a lot of the times where we're in. Um I'm going to do really anything in the world when 7-on-7 there's no live rush, it's not football. Um then when it comes to team aspect, you got to have the mindset of you have Jeffrey Simmons coming at you, so you can't sit back there and pity pat the ball. You got to get the one read, and you probably got to check it down the next play. So, it just depends on the situation, depends on what team period we're in, and you know, how I feel what route we have on um versus that coverage and how I need to throw it. >> When you're when you're in team period and 7-on-7, just being out there, like how much goes into just, okay, I'm trying something. I want to see if I can get this ball in that spot or get this ball to that guy. How much goes into that? every play, honestly. this is the time to do stuff that I do a lot in the game. Um it just depends, you know, what coverage our defense presents. Um our defense is real good at disguising. Um so, me seeing it faster and then already know what route I want to get to while I'm dropping back and then declaring whether I have to move in the pocket or not to get to the check down. So, it really just depends on what the defense has coverage-wise and we have to be able to react to it. >> is it on offense where you think you guys made the biggest strides in the off-season and what are the areas you got to be better at when training starts in July? >> I think our biggest stride is just the operation of everything. Everybody knows what to do um from up front all the way to the running backs room, everybody. Um I think the biggest thing that we can improve on is just continue to over-communicate. Make sure everyone knows what we're doing, even if it's a it's a threes guy that's not getting a lot of reps, make sure he knows what to do and then just continue to work on our timing with myself and the the backs and the receivers. >> What are your goals for what do you hope to improve the most personally from year one to year two and >> Um I think just far as a team uh to get a chance to be in the playoffs. Um try to make a run at it and then personally um just continue to be who I was last year, be an instinctive player, you know, be a great, you know, team leader um and win some games and then, you know, all the other stuff will take care of itself. >> Do you feel the pressure to get results this year given that the way the league works with first round picks usually if they don't get results by year three, there's a quarterback that's brought in for a competition and right now you haven't had that last year or this year. Do you feel that pressure to get the results and the wins and statistics and everything else? >> Um no. You win or lose. It's really that simple. It's either going to win today on the field or you're going to lose today day field. You're going to throw an incomplete pass or you're going to throw a complete pass. It's honestly that simple. Football's not hard. Um the pressure is the pressure we put on ourselves as people in the locker room. Um it's not whether or not we have a bad play. That's going to happen. I'm not going to go over there and go 50 for 50 every time. Um it's more just how we limit it um and not letting just one bad play carry through to the over as a whole collectively offensively. I'm just trying to limit that. I think if we do that we'll be one of the best offenses out there. >> So what is the pressure you're putting on yourself then? So what is the pressure you're putting on >> Uh just to be perfect. Um even though it's one of the hardest things to do in this world is be perfect. I want to be a perfect football player. Um and I think if I continue to strive to try and get that, you know, I'll be able to help this team win a lot of games. >> When you go watch the film when you go watch the film of these practices, do you find yourself scrutinizing the bad days more than the good days or or or not? >> Uh I never compliment myself. Um it's my job. Um I scrutinize the bad more than anything. I'm going to make good plays. I'm going to do a lot of good stuff. I know that. I did it every stop. I did it in high school when I threw the ball five times a game. So um it's it's more of just limiting everything and allowing everybody else to do their job. Me not having to do, you know, everything as far as me putting it on myself. Just more of let the receivers make the plays. Let the O line do their job. And if I do my job, everything else take care of itself. >> Cam, you were pretty adamant last year that even through all the combine stuff, all the workouts you did, that you weren't going to take much of a break from the end of mini camp to the start of training camp. Do you plan to do the same thing this year or how will you change things up to to best suit you for this season you think? >> Uh just got to go. Just got to work out. Just got to get up and go each and every day. You got 40 days till we start camp. So, you know, the break is from for us January to February, maybe early March. there there's no more time for breaks for nobody in the room. We just got to got to go. We're behind the eight ball. We finished with the number four pick last year. Our goal is not to be top 15 picks. We want to be later. That's that's means we get a chance at the playoffs. We get a chance to win the division. That's our goal each and every year. >> Coach Saleh said Cam, how important are these this two day stretch? Obviously you have the practice today tomorrow. Coach Saleh said this is essentially an extension of OTAs. But how important is this week especially with the veterans here on the field? >> Uh it's real good. Especially just for the connection with me with the receivers. The defense they're working on a lot of different coverages. So it's good that we're going to be able to see that. And then soft spots how I want guys to be with body language. How it feels from my point of view. And I think that's just all stuff that we'll continue to work out. And I think just the I'm happy that we're going to continue to keep going while a lot of people aren't doing it. That it's more reps. I think more reps equal you know better plays in the game is going to end up helping everybody. >> How much better do you have to be? You said the goal was to make the playoffs this year. How much better personally do you have to be this year than you were last year? >> I just think I got to be better every day. It's more it's not more of just being better each and every game. Just being consistent each and every game. Knowing who I'm playing up front. Knowing who I'm playing in the back end. Having good timing with my receivers like we've been having this whole OTAs and mini camp. And then when the when the when the lights get bright when the times get big you know we all got to lock in together like we've been doing out here and just make plays together. >> Excellent. >> Appreciate it. >> Hey Cam, say it to the camera. You want to get the guys home. >> [music]

title: Robert Saleh on Cam Ward, Titans Defense and Preparing for Training Camp
text: Coach, what were the conversations like yesterday talking to the team about expectations for the next couple days before the long break? >> Uh we we did that last week. Uh yesterday was more physicals and uh did a little staff uh uh team bonding uh exercise, but uh they know the uh expectations. We'll we'll hit those again on Thursday and just what they need to get done over the next 40 days and what we need to get done over the next 40 days to prepare ourselves for for the season. you had quite a bit of time leading up to this now where what have you learned about your football team as you get ready to get them all out here? >> Uh they're they'll do anything we ask. Um really good group of kids uh or young men I should say. And uh so I'm not we're not worried about that. But like I said it guys, it's from an OTAA standpoint. Anyone who thinks they know their football team after a bunch of bobbleheads running around with big helmets on it's um they're lying to you. Anybody uh have injuries or dings or concerns that'll keep them from being out there? >> Uh there's a couple guys that we're trying to work through here pre-activation to see where they're at, but uh otherwise we should have a full roster. >> When Cam misses like an open receiver, what's the why for him usually? Do you know? >> Um well, it's there there's always going to be a couple of things. whether or not he's trying to uh uh I shouldn't say force, but whether he's trying to hit tight windows um um you know, tying his feet. We talked about tying his feet uh uh into the progression of how he plays. Uh so there's a bunch of things that he's going through, but uh but overall, I mean, every quarterback is going to miss a couple here and there, but I think Cam's had done a really nice job throughout OTAAS. >> As you look back and see, you know, some of the inaccuracies, some of the good things, like how do you balance that? Oh, well, it's just OTAAS. there's still plenty of time to work, but then also like, hey, we got to get this right. >> Um, it it's a little bit of both where you're Yeah, they're all these guys are going to miss throws, whether it's uh and knock on wood, I've been around long enough, shoot, I I would say Brock Pur's one of the most accurate quarterbacks in all of football and he would miss a lot of throws and that's okay. Um, these guys are all working on a few things here and there, but as we get closer, as he gets more comfortable with the system, as he gets more comfortable with what he's being asked, uh, play in and play out, uh, the expectation is that he, uh, things start cleaning up. And so, what he's doing now, I think, like I said, I think he's had an outstanding OTAA. He's done a lot of really good things, especially in those move the ball periods. Um, and, uh, like everybody on this team, the expectation is that he continues to get better. Where do you guys stand uh with your progress on the option routes? To to layman's eye, it doesn't seem like many of the problems have been related to receivers read one thing and the quarterbacks read another thing. Where are you in the progress of of those kind of things? >> Uh all of it's just a work in progress. We're all, like I said, they're all getting uh with every passing day, they'll get more and more comfortable with one another. Uh the timing of it all, uh the things that they're being asked to do. So again, it's this is all time and reps, guys. We've had what uh nine practices, so we're not even close to where this team's going to get. >> What's the complexity level of that in terms of receivers and quarterbacks breeding things the same? >> Um, but it is complex, especially with the way defenses muddy up uh uh have grown the mu uh muddy up uh their their coverage systems. We muddy it up with our uh with our shell and our disguises, but uh um like I said, they're they're a heck of a lot better today than they were in week one uh first practice, and they'll continue to get better as the time goes. >> How have you seen Tate kind of stack his days in the practices and the reps that he's got? >> Um same with all the rookies. I'm going to kind of clump him into that in the sense that uh you know, they they get here, they're so out of shape and so they're just trying to get themselves physically uh caught up in that regard. and he's done a really nice job from a practice standpoint as they all have. Um and again, you know, they get here, they're five weeks behind in terms of not not just physically, but uh the mental part of it in terms of install. So, um all of them have done a really nice job, uh playing catch-up and and putting themselves in a position to compete. >> This has become Jeff's team the last couple years. Obviously, he just Kent came in last week. Are you looking forward to seeing kind of what he brings emotionally, leadership wise to the practice field for you these couple of days? >> Um, yeah. I mean, it's always good to have everybody out here, but I I think especially for the Dline in our system that it's not going to show up till training camp. Uh, there's just a different speed, a different level of violence. Um, the expectations of what we ask out of the O line and Dline. Um, once we get to training camp and the pads come on changes dramatically. uh the speed at the way we operate uh should should filter out to the skill guys in the back seven. So uh like I said, excited to have the guys out here, but again, we're just we're in shorts, so it's it's not going to really affect anything. >> So what's the goal for them then this week? The Dline specifically, what's what's the metric that you're using to measure? >> Uh should [snorts] just come out out here, get have a good have good couple of days of uh it's really individual because you're still going three/4er speed with regards to team work. Um but uh come in and compete, work your tail off an individual, get a good lift in and and get yourself ready to uh kickstart your 40 days. >> Where would you say you've made your biggest strides or or what's pleased you the most from April until now when you break camp? >> Um I'd just say the the way that I feel like our guys have absorbed the systems. Um you know, speaking from a defensive standpoint, I feel like our guys have done a really nice job. You know, we been such a heavy heavy match team. uh um at least this organization has and where our our system is more vision vision on the quarterback. And it took a few almost five practices for our guys to start really locking in on that quarterback to try to get uh uh and trusting their eyes in that regard and trusting that their bodies putting their bodies in certain positions will put them in position to make plays. And then obviously offensively um eliminating the mental errors, guys just operating faster um running routes at the depth they need to run them uh um and just working on the overall timing. So like the the way all three phases have absorbed the systems and and have grown from day one till now has been really good. >> How much will things change for Cam and and the targets with a more complete or or fully complete secondary on the field? Man, >> say that one time. How much will things change for Cam and the and the receivers with your full second day out there? I know you haven't had >> Yeah, it it we haven't at all. Um guys uh dealing with a couple of injuries here and there, but um it it should be more competitive, you know, and uh um you know, anytime you get good on good and and guys competing, it's the uh competition level will only elevate. >> In terms of the in terms >> in Yes. more of a follow up to his question. In terms of the secondary guys, what have you seen from guys like Caligan and Micah Robinson getting those reps with the ones that they normally wouldn't get? >> Heck yeah. No, any anytime, you know, I've said this before. Um there isn't a single guy in the locker room that thinks he's a backup. Uh there's not a doesn't think that if they got the opportunity to play that they can't produce at that same level. And it's our job to make sure that they're in position to make the plays that those that anyone can make. And uh you know a lot of times and I've said this before um and I'm not talking about the Jeffrey Simmons of the world uh your superstars but the difference between player A and Z in this league is very very very very small and uh so and and most of the time it's just a matter of getting an opportunity to go out there and compete. So the fact that those guys got a chance to get uh compete and get all these reps has been really good. I don't know how much following the situation with Britain Sorby. Just how would you evaluate a situation like that as a coach evaluating talent and do you address the whole gambling stuff with your team or do you kind of trust them to sort it out? >> Uh the it's part of the uh uh the NFL curriculum. They're educated on uh gambling every single year. Uh, I have no comment on the uh on the young man, but uh but I know the NFL does a really good job educating our players on what they can and can't do. >> What's your philosophy on this week sort of in general? Is it sort of a continuation? >> That's an extension of what he is. >> Is there any part of like a midterm process with these guys or just >> No, because you're still you're still limited to the same rules. Are you a kind of are you a kind of a random place in installation or are you at a particular place that you timed up for these two days? >> Yeah, the they're uh well uh both offensively and defensively we'll throw some wrinkles in there. You know, the the the idea is that your OTAAS in training camp match. They mirror in terms of your install schedule. Uh and so we've had nine practices. Um and usually you're in you have your install in between eight and 10 practices in. So this week is more like hey let's just try a couple of wrinkles here and there or just try to introduce a couple of things but for the most part everything's in >> for you personally like the interaction with with Cam Ward where like if you see something that that needs to be corrected and you and you correct that with him. How does that process how's that been and like what's some of your feedback that that you've gotten from him just as far as his ability to take that constructive criticism and apply it? >> He can he can take any criticism you throw at him. Um, you know, he's I I've said it before, he go he moves on to the next play very quickly. He wants to know what he needs to get done. He has no ego to him. So, just um he see if he if a lot of times he recognizes what the mistake was before you even get to him. Um but if you have a coaching point for him, he's very receptive to all of it. >> Thanks, guys. >> Appreciate you guys. Your third day, you're doing something.

title: John Fassel on Titans Special Teams, Joey Slye and Kickoff Return
text: Congrats to the Knicks. I told the guys this morning in the meeting I think all four of their wins they came back from double digits. In all five games they came back from double digits. So, we had a lot of conversations about comebacks this spring in our special teams meetings and it seemed like there was tons of them. The hockey game, you know, from 4-0. Anyways, sorry. Just It was fascinating to watch the teams just fight back. And so, we had We enjoyed that the whole last couple months just highlighting all the things. >> How much do you pull from other sports like to to cite, you know, examples of effort or stories for individuals, whatever it may be? >> Yeah, a lot. I think it's a lot of fun. We We talked about the horse race, Golden Temple. I think it was the Kentucky Derby where he was in last place, I don't know, 3/4 of the way through the race. And how he just kept going and kept going and kept going. And I showed the clip cuz NBC had a great clip where they zoomed from the top and showed him in last place, I don't know, halfway through. And he just kept going. He navigated the course and he ended up winning it. And so, that horse's name was Golden Temple. So, we have a new term for our kick return. Kick returners, when they catch the ball, about the tempo they want to run with. So, we call it a golden tempo. So, we pull from We pull from hockey. We pull from basketball. We watch the horse race. We watch all kinds of stuff. >> It's rare here anyway for there not to be a third leg in camp. You're pretty confident you won't have one. And and how does it change the >> Yeah, I actually preferred only having one snapper one kicker one punter through camp when you know they're the guy. And I'm pretty certain we have our guy. So, for them just to get all the work I think it's really important for them. And I'm not ever worried about training camp and volume cuz we can monitor the volume. You know, we get a jugs machine. So, the jugs machine can hit balls through returners that we need. So, I think it's important for Joey and Tommy and Morgan to get all the real work. And I can control the volume as far as not getting too much. So, um they're really damn good, and I'm excited about what they've done so far. >> Is the emphasis for Joey this year any different than what it was coming into last year? >> No. No, I think for him it's just continuing, probably like any kicker, to find the consistency. Because I and I'm not just saying this, I think his best ball is as good as anybody in the league. He hits a high trajectory ball, he hits a straight ball, he hits a far ball. And he can continue to find that on a consistent basis, I think he's one of the better ones in the league. And so, I have some goals for him, and he knows what they are, and I think they're lofty but very attainable. So, I'm looking forward to him having his best season. >> What difference in covering you got a lot You got a bunch of new guys on teams this year, but difference in covering punts for Townsend compared to for Hecker? >> Yeah. Uh I don't know yet. Yeah, we'll we'll see. I think they have some similarities and some differences. I think Tommy's an elite hangtime punter, and continue to work on the directional element with him. But when we're out there at practice so far, the guys that are protecting the punter and covering the punt, they don't really know what's happening. They never look at the punter, and they never see the ball. So, they just know what their duties are covering the punt, and they're looking at the returner the whole time. So, however the ball gets there, the guys who are covering and doing all the dirty work, they they don't know anything going on. They're just They're just going and you know, fighting. So, >> One of those guys is Bryce. >> Yeah. >> And I know he made a strong impression on you last year, but he got hurt. Is he back to where he was with you at this point? >> I think so. Last year at this point, he was coming off one or two little clean-up knee surgeries. So, he's ahead of where he was at this point last year right now. And I think it shows. You know, to have a whole off season of him competing and being full speed has has been different for him. Um he's cleared from his knee injury he had, you know, this past season. So, I'm looking forward to what Bryce can do. And I think the big part of Bryce's game is up in the ante for him on kick kick return. You know, he's a block destructor on kickoff and a front line blocker on kick return. And I think that's such a big element in our special teams game now is being able to perform on kickoff, where before it was touchbacks and so all you needed was guys that can run down there and fake it. Now you need real guys that can block destruct and play tackle football. And then the hardest element I think in all of football, offense, defense, special teams, is being a blocker on the front line of kickoff return. I'm biased, but I think that's probably the hardest skill to do. And it requires 10 of them for us on special teams. You got 10 guys in the front line and it's very difficult and um we need guys that can do that. So that's been a big emphasis for us also. >> guy at hitting the holes, finding it and and going. >> But when you evaluate other guys on special teams on their blocking ability, if they have a returner other than Jim who may not hit the hole the same way he does, how do you get a fair evaluation of those guys behind other returners? >> As far as like new guys we've signed, uh I haven't really looked into that too much. I think the tactics and techniques we use are a little bit different, maybe. So, everybody always gets a clean slate coming here. I think what you can really look at is you can look at, you know, a guy's willingness and ability to finish, you know, a guy's willingness to collide. Those are the things I think that mattered the most to me watching college tape or watching unrestricted free agent tape or picking somebody up off the street is you can you can see motor and physical skills and willingness to play and collide. Then everything else I think is my responsibility to teach them how to do it. Um but that's always the starting grounds I feel like cuz yeah, it's hard teaching front line blocking. It's very hard to teach it and it's very hard to be able to execute it and so a lot of our our stuff is match up driven to make sure we don't have a receiver put on a defensive end. And so um those are all the discussions that we had this morning and that we have every day that are a lot of fun to find the strengths of every one of our players and make sure that we put them in those spots of strengths and not necessarily consider any weakness. >> As you go through the process like watching other leagues, do you watch some of the special teams there and then have you ever like pulled something from XFL or you know, watching the EFL whatever it may be and applied it to your your strategy? >> Totally. Great question. Absolutely, yes. So when the first kickoff, you know, deal got done with us, I watched a ton of the XFL tape cuz they're really the ones that kind of started this new brand of kickoff. And so I broke down all 400 reps as far as watching every single player and the techniques that were used. And so I still go back to some of that tape and look at it just to see if what we're doing now has any match to what they were doing cuz it was fascinating tape to watch. You know, a new league just create something like that that now we're using. And then of course I watched a ton of USFL tape and it's not only for the schematics and the tactical but it's also the players, you know, and my previous stop, you know, we pulled two guys out of the USFL that were really damn good and that had to do with just watching for schematic and tactical purposes but also studying players. So I do I you know, look at college tape, XFL tape, USFL tape, UFL tape. Um haven't gotten to the arena honestly probably for a while so you can get a lot from just just watching. >> Thanks guys. >> Thanks for your time. >> Thanks you guys. >> Appreciate it. >> Have a great summer.

title: Brian Daboll Talks Cam Ward, Titans Offense and Minicamp Progress
text: last time that I met with you guys in terms of the installation. We've really thrown a lot at these guys. Plays, fundamentals, techniques, different types of huddle variations. They're doing a good job of picking it up. It's a normal OTA. Particularly a new one since our first season here. So, throwing a lot at these guys. They're doing a really good job. Going back into the meeting rooms, getting the corrections, improving on the things that we asked those guys to improve on. It's been a It's been an enjoyable time so far. The quarterbacks are doing a good job. They have a lot on their plate, but in terms of, you know, the overall operation of the offense, getting the play, getting to the line of scrimmage, handling Mike points, redirecting protections, signaling to receivers, their pocket movement I think has improved.
